```ts
}
```

**How consumers use it:** every component in this fragment opens with some destructure of `useTheme()` — `const { colors, colorScheme } = useTheme()` (Card `:53`, Button `:52`, GlassBottomSheet `:161`, Picker `:49`, GlassDot `:24`), `const { colors, isDark } = useTheme()` (TextInput `:41`, ScrollableTextInput `:98`, GlassAccentStrip `:37`), or `const { colors } = useTheme()` (RadioGroup `:39`, Checkbox `:34`, Switch `:39`, Banner `:46`). **154 files** in `src`/`app` reference `useTheme`.

**Mechanics:**

- Initial state from RN `useColorScheme()`: `systemColorScheme === 'dark' ? 'dark' : 'light'` (`:33-35`).
- Persisted under `AsyncStorage` key **`'app-color-scheme'`** (`:25`), read once on mount (`:42-44`, `loadThemePreference` `:46-58`); a stored value also calls `Appearance.setColorScheme(savedScheme)` (`:51`).
- `setColorScheme` (`:60-72`) updates state immediately, calls `Appearance.setColorScheme`, then persists fire-and-forget with a `logError` catch.
- `toggleTheme` (`:74-77`) flips light↔dark through `setColorScheme`.
- `deriveSchemeSlice(scheme)` (`:96-104`) is the **single** derivation of `{ colorScheme, colors: Colors[scheme], isDark: scheme === 'dark' }`, shared by `ThemeProvider`'s memo (`:81`) and `ForceColorScheme`'s (`:138`) so they cannot drift (PR-86 review L3).
- `ForceColorScheme` spreads the parent value then overrides only the scheme slice: **theme ACTIONS (`toggleTheme` / `setColorScheme`) pass through to the real provider**, so a settings control inside a forced subtree still works app-wide (`:120-129`).

**`ForceColorScheme` consumers** (9 files, all forcing dark): `src/features/documentation/notes/components/NotesSectionEditor.tsx`, `src/features/import/pdf-import/components/ImportTerminalProgress.tsx`, `src/features/media/media-library/components/MediaPreviewFullscreen.tsx`, `src/features/ocr-time-capture/components/{CameraControls,CameraInstructions,CameraPermissions,CameraScreen,CaptureButton,OcrCaptureFlow}.tsx`. Purpose (`:120-125`): "surfaces that are intentionally theme-invariant — e.g. terminal-style always-dark panels."

**What it replaced:** `loadThemePreference()` → `void loadThemePreference()` (`:43`); `.catch((error) =>` → `.catch((error: unknown) =>` (`:66`); trailing commas and multi-line import/`useMemo` reflow. `deriveSchemeSlice`, `ForceColorScheme`, the storage key and every derived field are **byte-identical to baseline**.

**For the demo:** this is the theming seam to replicate — one context supplying `{ colorScheme, colors, isDark }`, a persisted preference, and a nestable subtree override that flips `colors`/`isDark` while leaving the setters pointed at the real provider. There is **no third "system" state** in the value: `colorScheme` is always resolved to `'light'` or `'dark'`.

### `Header` — `src/components/layout/Header.tsx`

**Status:** CHANGED
**Phase/PR:** `55dd25d4 style(header): use the settings chevron for the wizard back control` (PR
#127) · `9ba41d5d fix(layout): token the header's platform padding and give MainHeader real targets`
(PR #123) · `d1739700 style: adopt prettier and reformat (886 files)` (PR #106).

**Role:** The WIZARD (form-flow) header — a title row with optional back / exit / drawer-menu
controls, in either a solid or a glass (LinearGradient + hairline + top highlight) treatment. Mounted
only by `FormLayout`.

**Canonical recipe NOW**

Platform inset constant (Header.tsx:150-151):

```ts
const HEADER_TOP_PADDING =
  Layout.headerPadding[Platform.OS as 'ios' | 'android'] ?? Layout.headerPadding.android
```
→ **iOS 50, Android 20**. Applied to BOTH the solid and glass containers (that duplication is
documented at Header.tsx:145-149: "the solid and glass variants each carried their own copy of the
ternary, so a change to one would silently fork the header from itself").

`StyleSheet.create` block, verbatim (Header.tsx:153-207):

```ts

  container: {
    paddingTop: HEADER_TOP_PADDING,
    borderBottomWidth: 1,

  // Glass wrapper for proper layering
  glassWrapper: {
    position: 'relative',
  },
  // Glass container with gradient
  glassContainer: {
    paddingTop: HEADER_TOP_PADDING,
    borderBottomWidth: 1,
  },
  // Top highlight edge for light reflection effect
  highlight: {
    position: 'absolute',

    minWidth: Layout.touchTarget.min,
```

### `MainHeader` — `src/components/layout/MainHeader.tsx`

**Status:** CHANGED
**Phase/PR:** `04f07956 feat(map): give the Map tab the shared floating header` (PR #125) ·
`b243da27 style(header): trim the glass band to just-below-flush with the title` (PR #125) ·
`afe4fd1a fix(layout): trim the Cases/Dashboard header from 92pt to 64pt` (PR #125) ·
`9ba41d5d fix(layout): token the header's platform padding and give MainHeader real targets` (PR #123).

**Role:** The TAB screens' header — a flat, transparent `3xl`-bold page title on the left with up to
two 44x44 icon buttons on the right. Never glass or solid on its own; it is the child of
`OverlayHeader` on all four tabs.

**Canonical recipe NOW** — full `StyleSheet.create` verbatim (MainHeader.tsx:105-165):

```ts
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  // Trimmed from 92pt of chrome to 64pt. The old geometry was
  // `paddingVertical: md` (16 top AND bottom), `minHeight: touchTarget.large`
  // (56) and `marginBottom: md` (16), which put the first list card at
  // `insets.top + 108` — about 15% of a tall display gone before any content.
  //
  // The padding is split top/bottom because the two edges want different
  // things: the title sits just under the status bar (the grid now runs to the
  // physical top, so there is no band to clear), while the bottom closes up
  // right beneath the row.
  container: {
    // No bottom margin: inside `OverlayHeader` a child margin inflates the
    // measured glass box, so the band ran 8pt past the content (owner: too much
    // blur under the title). The resting gap lives in the list spacer instead.
  },
  content: {
    flexDirection: 'row',
    alignItems: 'flex-end',
    paddingHorizontal: Layout.spacing.md,
    // `xs` rather than 0: one grid-unit of daylight keeps the 3xl title's
    // ascender off the status-bar glyphs, and still reads as "immediately
    // under".
    paddingTop: Layout.spacing.xs,
    // `xs` on both edges: the glass band should sit just-below-flush with the
    // title and icons (Sea People is the reference for how tight this reads).
    paddingBottom: Layout.spacing.xs,
    // `min` (44), not `large` (56). This is NOT a touch target — the two icon
    // buttons carry their own 44x44 boxes below and are untouched by this
    // change. At 56 it was a floor ABOVE the row's natural height (the 44pt
    // buttons already govern it), so it was padding wearing a different name.
    minHeight: Layout.touchTarget.min,
  },
  title: {
    flex: 1,
    fontSize: Typography.fontSize['3xl'],
    fontWeight: Typography.fontWeight.bold,
  },
  actionsContainer: {
    flexDirection: 'row',
    alignItems: 'center',
    gap: Layout.spacing.base,
  },
  // 24px icon plus `spacing.xs` of padding left these at 32x32, against the
  // project's 44x44 minimum, and both are primary entry points (New Case, and
  // the only route to Settings). A real 44x44 box rather than `hitSlop`,
  // because the accessibility inspector measures the frame and several other
  // undersized targets in this codebase are rescued by `hitSlop` in a way that
  // is invisible in the stylesheet.
  newCaseButton: {
    minWidth: Layout.touchTarget.min,
    minHeight: Layout.touchTarget.min,
    alignItems: 'center',
    justifyContent: 'center',
  },
  settingsButton: {
    minWidth: Layout.touchTarget.min,
    minHeight: Layout.touchTarget.min,
    alignItems: 'center',
    justifyContent: 'center',
  },
})
```

Resolved: `container` is an **empty rule** (no margin at all). `content` = `row / align-items:flex-end /
paddingHorizontal 16 / paddingTop 4 / paddingBottom 4 / minHeight 44`. `title` = `flex 1 / 30px / 700`,
colour `colors.text` (MainHeader.tsx:67). `actionsContainer` = `row / centre / gap 12`. Both icon
buttons = `44x44 centred`, no padding.

Icons (MainHeader.tsx:83, 96), both `size={24}` `color={colors.primary}`:

- New Case: `<Ionicons name="folder-open-outline" size={24} color={colors.primary} />`
- Settings: `<Ionicons name="settings-outline" size={24} color={colors.primary} />`

Both are conditional on their handler being passed. `onSettingsPress` is now **optional**
(MainHeader.tsx:26) — "the Map and Export tabs have no settings surface of their own, and an
actionless title row is a valid header rather than a missing one" (MainHeader.tsx:22-25).

testIDs: `testID` on the container, `` `${testID}-new-case-button` ``,
`` `${testID}-settings-button` `` (both `undefined` if no `testID` given).

**What it replaced** (`git show d9606460:src/components/layout/MainHeader.tsx`)

```ts
container:  { marginBottom: Layout.spacing.md },              // 16 → REMOVED entirely
content:    { …, paddingVertical: Layout.spacing.md,          // 16 top AND bottom
              minHeight: Layout.touchTarget.large },          // 56 → 44
actionsContainer: { …, gap: 12 },                             // raw literal → Layout.spacing.base
newCaseButton:  { padding: Layout.spacing.xs },               // 4 → 32x32 box → real 44x44
settingsButton: { padding: Layout.spacing.xs },               // 4 → 32x32 box → real 44x44
```
`onSettingsPress` was a REQUIRED prop at baseline.

Total chrome: **92pt → 64pt** at `afe4fd1a` (16+16 padding + 56 floor + 16 margin put the first list
card at `insets.top + 108`), then `b243da27` cut `paddingBottom` `sm`(8) → `xs`(4) and deleted the
`marginBottom: sm`(8) that `afe4fd1a` had left, moving that 8pt into the list spacers
(`Layout.spacing.sm` → `Layout.spacing.md`, i.e. `headerHeight + 8` → `headerHeight + 16` at
`app/(tabs)/cases.tsx:1140` and `app/(tabs)/home.tsx:280`). Net resting position shifts up by exactly
the 4pt actually trimmed. The pinned spacer height in the cases integration test moved `64` → `72`.

**Consumers / mount points:** all four tabs, always wrapped in `OverlayHeader`:

- `app/(tabs)/cases.tsx:1120-1125` — `title="Cases"`, both `onNewCasePress` and `onSettingsPress`, `testID="cases-header"`
- `app/(tabs)/home.tsx:374-378` — `title="Dashboard"`, `onSettingsPress` only, `testID="dashboard-header"`
- `app/(tabs)/map.tsx:213` — `<MainHeader title="Case Maps" testID="map-header" />`, no actions
- `app/(tabs)/export.tsx:204` — `<MainHeader title="Export" testID="export-header" />`, no actions

**Notes:** MainHeader.tsx:34-54 is the standing ruling that tab headers deliberately do NOT take
`Header`'s glass or solid treatment, for three structural reasons: (1) `Header` owns the status-bar
inset and the tab screens have their own safe-area wrapper, so it would double; (2) this is a `3xl`
page TITLE that scrolls over `GridBackground`, and a bordered glass band "would cut the grid in half
and read as a stuck toolbar"; (3) they share no call site. "What they SHOULD share, and now do, is the
44pt touch target on their icon buttons." The `b243da27` band tightness ruling names **Sea People** as
the owner's reference.

### `ModalHeader` — `src/components/layout/ModalHeader.tsx`

**Status:** NEW since baseline (file does not exist at `d9606460`)
**Phase/PR:** `f9b0b2a1 refactor(components): extract the five copied page-sheet headers into ModalHeader` (PR #122).

**Role:** The one page-sheet glass header — a horizontal row of `[accent icon] [title] [close ✕]` on
the `elevated` glass gradient with a hairline bottom border. Rendered by five modals as the first
child of their own `GridBackground` inside their own `SafeAreaView`.

**Canonical recipe NOW** — full render (ModalHeader.tsx:54-79) and styles (ModalHeader.tsx:81-97):

```tsx
const { colors, colorScheme } = useTheme()
const glassStyle = GlassColors[colorScheme].elevated

<LinearGradient
  colors={[...glassStyle.gradient]}
  start={{ x: 0, y: 0 }}
  end={{ x: 0, y: 1 }}
  style={[styles.header, { borderBottomColor: glassStyle.border }]}
  testID={testID}
>
  <Ionicons name={icon} size={Layout.iconSize.md} color={colors.primary} />
  <Text style={[styles.title, { color: colors.text }]}>{title}</Text>
  <Pressable
    onPress={onClose}
    style={styles.closeButton}
    // The glyph plus its padding is a 32x32 frame. `hitSlop` takes it to
    // 52x52, clear of the 44 minimum, without growing the header by 20px
    // the way a real 44x44 frame would. Same value as `SettingsNavBar`.
    hitSlop={10}
    accessibilityRole="button"
    accessibilityLabel={closeAccessibilityLabel}
    testID={closeTestID}
  >
    <Ionicons name="close" size={Layout.iconSize.md} color={colors.textSecondary} />
  </Pressable>
</LinearGradient>
```

```ts
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  header: {
    flexDirection: 'row',
    alignItems: 'center',
    padding: Layout.spacing.lg,
    borderBottomWidth: 1,
    gap: Layout.spacing.sm,
  },
  title: {
    fontSize: Typography.fontSize['2xl'],
    fontWeight: Typography.fontWeight.bold,
    flex: 1,
  },
  closeButton: {
    padding: Layout.spacing.xs,
  },
})
```

Resolved: `header` = `row / centre / padding 24 all sides / borderBottomWidth 1 / gap 8`.
`title` = `24px / 700 / flex 1`, colour `colors.text`. `closeButton` = `padding 4` (→ 32x32 frame)
plus `hitSlop={10}` (→ 52x52 effective). Leading icon and close glyph are both **24px**
(`Layout.iconSize.md`); leading icon takes `colors.primary`, close takes `colors.textSecondary`
(light `#4b5563` / dark `#99badd`).

Both theme branches (`GlassColors[colorScheme].elevated`):

| | light | dark |
|---|---|---|
| gradient (vertical) | `rgba(255,255,255,1)` → `rgba(248,250,252,1)` | `rgba(23,65,110,0.88)` → `rgba(14,57,101,0.95)` |
| `borderBottomColor` | `rgba(100,116,139,0.35)` | `rgba(43,140,193,0.25)` |

Prop list: `icon` (Ionicons name), `title`, `onClose`, `closeAccessibilityLabel` (**required**, not
defaulted), `closeTestID?`, `testID?`.

**What it replaced:** nothing at this path. It is the extraction of five byte-for-byte identical
inline headers — `UserProfileModal`, `EnrollDeviceModal`, `ProvisioningWizardModal`,
`EnrollmentQRModal`, `UserManagementModal` — which "shipped this header byte-for-byte identically:
the same `elevated` gradient, the same `row / center / padding.lg / gap.sm` block, the same 24px
accent icon, the same `2xl`-bold flexed title and the same 4px-padded close glyph" (ModalHeader.tsx:4-9).

**Consumers / mount points** (all via the barrel `import { ModalHeader } from '@/components/layout'`):

- `src/features/agency-cloud/components/EnrollDeviceModal.tsx:285`
- `src/features/agency-cloud/components/EnrollmentQRModal.tsx:45`
- `src/features/agency-cloud/components/ProvisioningWizardModal.tsx:192`
- `src/features/agency-cloud/components/UserManagementModal.tsx:317`
- `src/features/settings/user-profile/components/UserProfileModal.tsx:137`

**Notes:**
- ModalHeader.tsx:13-15: "deliberately NOT a safe-area component and NOT flexed: every caller renders
  it as the first child of `GridBackground` inside its own `SafeAreaView`".
- ModalHeader.tsx:32-37 cites **DEF-UI-006** for why `closeAccessibilityLabel` is required rather
  than defaulted to "Close": five near-identical page sheets all announcing "Close" are
  indistinguishable to a screen-reader user (the regression DEF-UI-006 records for
  `GlassBottomSheet`'s hardcoded scrim label).
- ModalHeader.tsx:67-69: the `hitSlop={10}` choice is explicitly cheaper than a real 44x44 frame,
  which would grow the header by 20px; "Same value as `SettingsNavBar`".

### `OverlayHeader` — `src/components/layout/OverlayHeader.tsx`

**Status:** NEW since baseline (file does not exist at `d9606460`)
**Phase/PR:** all in PR #125 — `4c0116cf feat(layout): EXPERIMENTAL floating header for Cases and
Dashboard` → `ad265566 fix(layout): degrade the floating header to gradient when blur is not in the
binary` → `9b2b1d71 feat(layout): make the floating header materialize on scroll, to the screen edge`
→ `4d064e2a fix(layout): let the scroll surface reach y=0 so the glass has content to blur`. Extended
to the Map tab by `04f07956 feat(map)` (also PR #125).

**Role:** A WRAPPER that lifts a header out of flow and floats it over the scrolling list, so content
passes underneath and fades behind a scroll-linked translucent band that reaches the physical top of
the screen. It composes whatever header it is given (always `MainHeader`), owns only the backdrop and
the height measurement, and touches nothing inside its child.

**Canonical recipe NOW**

Module constants (OverlayHeader.tsx:59, 69, 101-104):

```ts
const BLUR_INTENSITY = 40
const MATERIALIZE_AT = 20     // px of scroll over which the glass fades in
const DIM = {
  blurred: [0.55, 0.35, 0],
  plain:   [0.92, 0.72, 0],
} as const
```

Platform / capability fork (OverlayHeader.tsx:91-93, 140-141):

```ts
function hasNativeBlurView(): boolean {
  return requireOptionalNativeModule('ExpoBlurView') !== null
}
const useBlur = Platform.OS === 'ios' && hasNativeBlurView()
const ramp = useBlur ? DIM.blurred : DIM.plain
```

Materialize animation (OverlayHeader.tsx:148-150) — a static blur crossfaded by **opacity only**,
never an animated `intensity`:

```ts
const materialStyle = useAnimatedStyle(() => ({
  opacity: interpolate(scrollY.get(), [0, MATERIALIZE_AT], [0, 1], Extrapolation.CLAMP),
}))
```

Render (OverlayHeader.tsx:152-196):

```tsx
<View
  style={[styles.overlay, { paddingTop: insets.top }]}
  onLayout={handleLayout}
  testID={testID}
>
  <Animated.View
    pointerEvents="none"
    style={[StyleSheet.absoluteFill, materialStyle]}
    testID={testID ? `${testID}-material` : undefined}
  >
    {useBlur && (
      <BlurView
        intensity={BLUR_INTENSITY}
        tint={isDark ? 'dark' : 'light'}
        style={StyleSheet.absoluteFill}
        testID={testID ? `${testID}-blur` : undefined}
      />
    )}
    <LinearGradient
      colors={[
        withAlpha(colors.background, ramp[0]),
        withAlpha(colors.background, ramp[1]),
        withAlpha(colors.background, ramp[2]),
      ]}
      locations={[0, 0.65, 1]}
      style={StyleSheet.absoluteFill}
      testID={testID ? `${testID}-dim` : undefined}
    />
  </Animated.View>
  {children}
</View>
```

Styles, verbatim (OverlayHeader.tsx:199-210):

```ts
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  // Out of flow, pinned to the top of whatever it is mounted in — which is
  // `Screen`'s inset layer, so it starts below the status bar and the grid
  // still runs to the physical top behind it.
  overlay: {
    position: 'absolute',
    top: 0,
    left: 0,
    right: 0,
    zIndex: 10,
  },
})
```

**Resolved dim gradient, all four combinations** (3 stops, `locations` `[0, 0.65, 1]`, vertical):

| | stop 0 (top) | stop 0.65 | stop 1 (bottom) |
|---|---|---|---|
| iOS+blur, dark (`#002853`) | `rgba(0, 40, 83, 0.55)` | `rgba(0, 40, 83, 0.35)` | `rgba(0, 40, 83, 0)` |
| iOS+blur, light (`#ffffff`) | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.55)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.35)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0)` |
| plain (Android, or iOS w/o module), dark | `rgba(0, 40, 83, 0.92)` | `rgba(0, 40, 83, 0.72)` | `rgba(0, 40, 83, 0)` |
| plain, light | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.92)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.72)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0)` |

`BlurView` is iOS-only, `intensity={40}`, `tint` = `'dark'`/`'light'` following `isDark`.

Props: `children` (rendered untouched, above the backdrop), `onHeightChange: (height: number) => void`
(fired on every `onLayout`; the reported height **already includes** `insets.top` because the padding
is on the box), `scrollY: SharedValue<number>` (UI-thread scroll offset, written by the caller's
`useAnimatedScrollHandler`), `testID?`.

**What it replaced:** nothing — new file. The header it floats used to sit in flow inside the tab
screens. The revert path is documented at the call sites: "Revert the commit that introduced
`OverlayHeader` to get the flat in-flow header back — nothing inside `MainHeader` changed"
(`app/(tabs)/cases.tsx:1112-1114`).

**Consumers / mount points** — all four tabs, each inside a `Screen` with `excludeTopSafeArea={true}`:

- `app/(tabs)/cases.tsx:1115-1126` — `testID="cases-overlay-header"`; list spacer
  `<View style={{ height: headerHeight + Layout.spacing.md }} />` at `cases.tsx:1140`
- `app/(tabs)/home.tsx:369-379` — `testID="dashboard-overlay-header"`; spacer at `home.tsx:280`
- `app/(tabs)/map.tsx:206-214` — `testID="map-overlay-header"`; spacer passed as
  `ListHeaderComponent` to `MapPicker` at `map.tsx:218`
- `app/(tabs)/export.tsx:198-205` — `testID="export-overlay-header"`; `ExportHub` gets
  `contentTopInset={headerHeight}` at `export.tsx:208`

**Notes** (all in-file):
- OverlayHeader.tsx:2 — "EXPERIMENTAL, pending a device verdict". The Claude app's chat header is the
  named reference (:6).
- OverlayHeader.tsx:9-12 — the glass is SCROLL-LINKED: "at rest there is no material at all … and it
  materializes over the first `MATERIALIZE_AT` px of scroll, driven on the UI thread. And it reaches
  the physical top of the screen rather than stopping at the safe-area inset."
- OverlayHeader.tsx:20-34 — the platform fork is deliberate, not an oversight: iOS gets one `BlurView`
  at moderate intensity plus a light gradient dim; **Android gets NO blur**, gradient only, weighted
  heavier to compensate. Reason: `expo-blur` on Android renders via a semi-transparent overlay on old
  versions and a genuine render-effect on API 31+, and "a full-width blur repainting on every scroll
  frame is exactly the battery-and-thermals cost CLAUDE.md's performance rules tell us not to spend on
  decoration. Revisit only with a frame-time measurement in hand."
- OverlayHeader.tsx:36-37 — "The grid is intentionally NOT dimmed away — it shows through the band,
  which is the point of the translucency."
- OverlayHeader.tsx:63-68 — why `MATERIALIZE_AT = 20`: it "has to finish before anything legible
  reaches the title", and the first card is `headerHeight + spacing.sm` down.
- OverlayHeader.tsx:71-89 — `requireOptionalNativeModule('ExpoBlurView')` is permanent, not
  scaffolding: a dev client built before `expo-blur` was added would otherwise render RN's
  "Unimplemented component: <ViewManagerAdapter_ExpoBlurView_…>" banner instead of a header. Carries a
  `ponytail:` marker at :89 ("uncached on purpose; memoize only if a profile ever shows it").
- OverlayHeader.tsx:143-147 — never animate `intensity`: on Android it maps to `setBlurRadius` and
  re-renders the blur every frame; opacity of the whole material layer is free.
- OverlayHeader.tsx:154-160 — `paddingTop: insets.top` (not margin) so the header BOX starts at the
  physical top while its content sits below the status bar, "and `onLayout` therefore reports a height
  that already includes the inset, which is what keeps the list spacer correct with no arithmetic".

| complete / light | `#10b981` | `rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.65)` | `#10b981` | `rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.4)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.7)` |
| complete / dark | `#10d177` | `rgba(16, 209, 119, 0.65)` | `#10d177` | `rgba(16, 209, 119, 0.35)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.25)` |

**Media accordion** (CustomDrawerContent.tsx:288-432):

- Container `cameraActionContainer` = `paddingHorizontal 8 / paddingTop 16 / paddingBottom 4`;
  wrapper `marginVertical 4`.
- Header row `cameraButton` — identical recipe to `drawerItem` (`paddingVertical 16 /
  paddingHorizontal 24 / borderRadius 12 / borderWidth 1 / minHeight 56`, card gradient + border +
  `borderTopColor` highlight + card shadow). Icon `albums-outline` `size={24}` on
  `colors.textSecondary`, `marginRight 16`; label "Media" `16px / 500` on `colors.text`.
- Chevron `<Ionicons name="chevron-down" size={20} color={colors.textSecondary} />` inside an
  `Animated.View` rotating **0° → 180°** (`interpolate(chevronProgress, [0,1], [0,180])`,
  CustomDrawerContent.tsx:117-123), spring `{ damping: 18, stiffness: 140, mass: 0.8 }`
  (CustomDrawerContent.tsx:98-102).
- Height animation: `withTiming(next ? measuredHeight : 0, { duration: ACCORDION_DURATION,
  easing: Easing.inOut(Easing.quad) })`. `ACCORDION_DURATION = 250` (:41),
  `SCROLL_AFTER_EXPAND_DELAY = 280` (:45), `MEDIA_CONTENT_FALLBACK_HEIGHT = 164` (:38).
  Measured height is `layout.height + Layout.spacing.sm` (:77).
- Sub-item container `marginLeft 16 / marginTop 8`. Each `mediaSubItem` = `paddingVertical 8 /
  paddingHorizontal 16 / borderRadius 12 / borderWidth 1 / minHeight 48 / marginBottom 4`, same card
  gradient + border + `borderTopColor` + card shadow. Sub-item icons `size={20}` on
  `colors.textSecondary`, `marginRight 16`; label `14px / 500 / flex 1` on `colors.text`.
- Three sub-items: `camera` → "Capture Media" (gated on `useStepVisible('media-capture')`),
  `mic` → "Record Audio" (gated on `useStepVisible('audio-recording')`),
  `folder-open-outline` → "Media Library" (ungated).

**Scroll content:** `paddingTop 8 / paddingBottom 24`, `showsVerticalScrollIndicator={false}`.

**Footer** (CustomDrawerContent.tsx:436-458) — `LinearGradient` with the header gradient
**REVERSED** (`[...glassHeaderStyle.gradient].reverse()`), `borderTopColor: glassHeaderStyle.border`,
`borderTopWidth: 1`, `paddingHorizontal 24 / paddingVertical 16 / alignItems: 'center'`. Two lines,
both on **`colors.textSecondary`**: "DVR Extraction Notes" at `14px / 500`, and
`v{Constants.expoConfig?.version || '1.0.0'}` at `12px`, `marginTop 4`.

Resolved footer gradient: light `rgba(248,250,252,0.95)` → `rgba(255,255,255,0.98)`;
dark `rgba(2,46,89,0.98)` → `rgba(0,38,80,0.95)`.

**What it replaced** (`git show d9606460:…`)

- `closeButton` was `{ padding: Layout.spacing.xs }` → ~36x36 (the header close glyph is 28px). Now a
  real 44x44 box.
- `backLink` had **no `borderWidth`** and was painted with a flat
  `style={[styles.backLink, { backgroundColor: colors.backgroundSecondary }]}` on the
  `TouchableOpacity` itself — light `#f9fafb`, dark `#0e3965`. Label sat on `colors.textSecondary`.
  It is now a `LinearGradient` on the card tier with border + lit top edge + card shadow, and the
  label moved to `colors.text`. Its radius (`md`/8), paddings (`8` / `16`), `minHeight` (`46`), the
  `arrow-back` glyph on `textSecondary`, and the divider beneath are all **deliberately unchanged**.
- `drawerItem`, `cameraButton`, `mediaSubItem` all had `borderRadius: Layout.borderRadius.md` (**8**)
  → now `Layout.borderRadius.lg` (**12**), per D13(a).
- All four glass row types carried only `{ borderColor: glassStyle.border }` — no
  `borderTopColor: glassStyle.highlightTop` and **no `Layout.shadow.card[colorScheme]`** at all.
- Footer text and version were on `colors.textTertiary`.
- `GlassColors[colorScheme ?? 'light']` → `GlassColors[colorScheme]` (dead fallback deleted, `2b60f679`).
- `Layout.drawerHeaderPadding[…] || …android` was already tokenised at baseline (only re-wrapped by
  prettier).

**Consumers / mount points:** one — `app/(form)/_layout.tsx:7` (import), `_layout.tsx:421-435`
(rendered inside an `ErrorBoundary` whose fallback is the local `DrawerErrorFallback`).

**Notes:**
- CustomDrawerContent.tsx:241-247: the lit edge is delivered as `borderTopColor` (two style keys)
  rather than a wrapper View plus an absolutely-positioned 1px strip — "`Card` needs the strip because
  its gradient is clipped by an `overflow: 'hidden'` container; these rows have no such container, so
  a `borderTopColor` IS the highlight edge and is the idiom `Button` and `GpsCaptureControl` already
  use."
- CustomDrawerContent.tsx:522-525: ruling **D13(a)** — top-level cards in a list go at `lg`, not `md`.
  "Three row types carried the same wrong radius."
- CustomDrawerContent.tsx:442-451 (contrast numbers, quoted): the footer paints the header gradient
  REVERSED, not `colors.card`, which is the ground the audit measured its **4.2:1** against; "on the
  real ground the tertiary token is **4.94 dark** and … **4.63 light** … both clear AA, but only just,
  at 14px and 12px." After the move to `textSecondary`: "**6.79 dark / 7.24 light**".
- `adf84775` commit body: both new pins are COMPARATIVE (back link vs a sibling item) rather than
  literal, because the test file stubs `@/constants/Colors` with a grey palette that has no
  `highlightTop`. Also records a mock defect removed — a local `expo-linear-gradient` mock that
  forwarded only `testID`/`style` and dropped `colors`, making every gradient in the drawer suite
  unobservable (BUG-003 inline-mock rule).
- CustomDrawerContent.tsx:139-147: BUG-011 — `router.dismissTo('/(tabs)/cases')`, never push/replace
  across the `(tabs)`/`(form)` boundary.

### `Screen` — `src/components/layout/Screen.tsx`

**Status:** CHANGED
**Phase/PR:** `4d064e2a fix(layout): let the scroll surface reach y=0 so the glass has content to blur`
(PR #125) · `ef3dfbe3 fix(layout): take the grid edge-to-edge behind the status bar` (PR #125) ·
`d2bbb8c7 chore(layout): Screen.tsx hygiene … plain ScrollView for non-form scroll [P7]` (PR #94) ·
`f61c9d42 perf(layout): focus-gate the scan line and cancel its infinite loop [P2]` (PR #94) ·
`d1739700 style: adopt prettier` (PR #106).

**Role:** The universal screen shell — an opaque themed container, an optional `GridBackground`, and
one of four content surfaces (keyboard-aware scroll, keyboard-aware non-scroll, plain `ScrollView`,
static `View`), with the safe-area inset applied to an inner layer rather than the container.

**Canonical recipe NOW**

```ts
// Screen.tsx:80-86
const paddingStyle: ViewStyle = padding
  ? {
      paddingHorizontal: Layout.screenPadding.horizontal,   // 16
      paddingTop: Layout.spacing.sm,                        // 8
      paddingBottom: Layout.spacing.md,                     // 16
    }
  : {}

// Screen.tsx:90-97
const safeAreaStyle: ViewStyle = safeArea
  ? {
      paddingTop: excludeTopSafeArea ? 0 : insets.top,
      paddingBottom: excludeBottomSafeArea ? 0 : insets.bottom,
      paddingLeft: insets.left,
      paddingRight: insets.right,
    }
  : {}

// Screen.tsx:99-109
const scrollContentStyle: ViewStyle = {
  flexGrow: 1,
  backgroundColor: showGrid ? 'transparent' : colors.background,
  ...paddingStyle,
}
const nonScrollContainerStyle: ViewStyle = {
  flex: 1,
  backgroundColor: showGrid ? 'transparent' : colors.background,
  ...paddingStyle,
}
```

Layering (Screen.tsx:188-206), the shape parity work has to reproduce:

```tsx
const insetContent = <View style={[styles.insetLayer, safeAreaStyle]}>{screenContent}</View>

return (
  <View style={[styles.container, { backgroundColor: colors.background }]} testID={testID}>
    {showGrid ? (
      <GridBackground gridOpacity={gridOpacity} showScanLine={showScanLine && isFocused}>
        {insetContent}
      </GridBackground>
    ) : (
      insetContent
    )}
  </View>
)
```

```ts
const styles = StyleSheet.create({                    // Screen.tsx:210-220
  container: {
    flex: 1,
  },
  // Carries `safeAreaStyle`. Inert (`flex: 1`, no padding) whenever
  // `safeArea={false}` - which is how `FormLayout` mounts this, because the
  // wizard's `Header` owns its own status-bar inset via `Layout.headerPadding`.
  insetLayer: {
    flex: 1,
  },
})
```

Prop defaults (Screen.tsx:51-68): `scrollable = true`, `padding = true`, `safeArea = true`,
`excludeBottomSafeArea = false`, **`excludeTopSafeArea = false`**, `keyboardAware = true`,
`showGrid = true`, `gridOpacity = 'subtle'`, `showScanLine = true`.

Content-surface testIDs: `` `${testID}-keyboard-scroll` ``, `` `${testID}-keyboard-noscroll` ``,
`` `${testID}-scroll` ``, `` `${testID}-static` ``. `KeyboardAwareScrollView` uses
`bottomOffset={40}`; all scroll surfaces use `showsVerticalScrollIndicator={false}`, `bounces={true}`,
`alwaysBounceVertical={false}`.

**What it replaced**

- `excludeTopSafeArea` did not exist; `safeAreaStyle.paddingTop` was unconditionally `insets.top`.
- The inset was on the **container**: `<View style={[styles.container, { backgroundColor:
  colors.background }, safeAreaStyle]}>`, with `GridBackground` as its child. Screen.tsx:177-187
  records why that was wrong: "a child cannot paint into its parent's padding, so the grid began at
  `insets.top` and the status-bar band showed the container's flat `colors.background` instead. That
  band was never a surface of its own; it was the parent showing through where the grid was not
  allowed to reach."
- `styles.insetLayer` is new.
- The non-keyboard-aware scrollable branch was `<KeyboardAwareScrollView … enabled={false}>` → now a
  plain `ScrollView` with the same props and the same testID contract.
- `showScanLine` was passed straight through (`showScanLine={showScanLine}`) → now
  `showScanLine={showScanLine && isFocused}`.

**Consumers / mount points:** `FormLayout` (`src/components/layout/FormLayout.tsx:77-90`,
`safeArea={false}`) plus the tab screens and most standalone screens directly. The four tabs pass
`excludeTopSafeArea={true}` (`cases.tsx:1107`, `home.tsx:362`, `map.tsx:200`, `export.tsx:192`),
always with `showGrid={true}` and `showScanLine={true}`.

**Notes:** Screen.tsx:23-36 documents `excludeTopSafeArea` in terms of the blur: "a `BlurView` can
only blur what is rendered beneath it, so if the list's frame stops at `insets.top` the glass above
that line samples bare background and scrolled content appears to be sliced off at a hard horizontal
edge instead of blurring off the top of the screen." Screen.tsx:193-199: the scan-line focus gate
lives in `Screen`, not `GridBackground`, "because `GridBackground` also renders outside a navigation
container (e.g. `LockScreen`), where `useIsFocused` would throw."

### `FormLayout` — `src/components/layout/FormLayout.tsx`

**Status:** UNCHANGED (formatting only — `d1739700 style: adopt prettier`)
**Phase/PR:** none since baseline beyond the repo-wide prettier pass.

**Role:** The wizard screen composition — a themed flex container holding `Header` (glass by default)
above a `Screen` with `safeArea={false}`. Every `(form)` route body renders through it.

**Canonical recipe NOW** — it defines no `StyleSheet`; the only style is inline (FormLayout.tsx:66):

```tsx
<View style={{ flex: 1, backgroundColor: colors.background }} testID={testID}>
  <Header
    title={title}
    showBack={!showExit}
    showExit={showExit}
    showMenu
    onBackPress={onBack}
    onExitPress={onExit}
    glass={glassHeader}
  />
  <Screen
    scrollable={scrollable}
    padding
    safeArea={false}
    keyboardAware={keyboardAware}
    showScanLine={showScanLine}
    testID={`${testID}-content`}
    …
  >
    {children}
  </Screen>
</View>
```

Defaults (FormLayout.tsx:47-62): `showExit = false`, **`glassHeader = true`**,
**`showScanLine = false`** ("Disabled by default for form screens (less distracting)"),
`keyboardAware = true`, `scrollable = true`.

Note the two derived flags: `showBack={!showExit}` and `showMenu` is **always on**.

**What it replaced:** nothing — semantically identical to baseline.

**Consumers / mount points:** the `(form)` wizard screens.

**Notes:** `safeArea={false}` is load-bearing and is explained from the other side, in
`Screen.tsx:214-216`: "`FormLayout` mounts this [with `safeArea={false}`] because the wizard's
`Header` owns its own status-bar inset via `Layout.headerPadding`."

### `GridBackground` — `src/components/layout/GridBackground.tsx`

**Status:** CHANGED
**Phase/PR:** `53429cb8 fix(theme): purge the pre-recolor teal accent and route the grid through
tokens` (PR #115) · `68f4e18a feat(theme): land the in-flight badge-blue recolor base` (PR #110) ·
`290f57d4 perf(layout): rasterize the grid only while the scan line animates [P5]` (PR #94) ·
`f61c9d42 perf(layout): focus-gate the scan line … [P2]` (PR #94) · `d1739700` prettier.

**Role:** The blueprint grid — an SVG `Pattern` of 1px lines at a 40px pitch, an optional animated
scan line sweeping top-to-bottom, and the children on top. Rendered by `Screen` (when `showGrid`) and
directly by `LockScreen` and the five modals that host `ModalHeader`.

**Canonical recipe NOW**

Defaults (GridBackground.tsx:29-36): `gridSize = 40`, `gridOpacity = 'subtle'`, `showScanLine = true`.

Colour resolution (GridBackground.tsx:75-87):

```ts
const gridColor = {
  subtle: colors.gridSubtle,
  normal: colors.grid,
  strong: colors.gridLight,
}[gridOpacity]

const scanLineTint = {
  backgroundColor: withAlpha(colors.primary, 0.3),
  shadowColor: colors.primary,
}
```

Resolved:

| `gridOpacity` | light | dark |
|---|---|---|
| `subtle` (default) | `rgba(30, 58, 138, 0.06)` | `rgba(153, 186, 221, 0.11)` |
| `normal` | `rgba(30, 58, 138, 0.10)` | `rgba(153, 186, 221, 0.14)` |
| `strong` | `rgba(30, 58, 138, 0.18)` | `rgba(153, 186, 221, 0.20)` |

Scan-line tint resolved: light `backgroundColor: rgba(30, 58, 138, 0.3)` / `shadowColor: #1e3a8a`;
dark `backgroundColor: rgba(43, 140, 193, 0.3)` / `shadowColor: #2B8CC1`.

SVG (GridBackground.tsx:104-119): `<Svg width="100%" height="100%" style={StyleSheet.absoluteFill}>`
with `<Pattern id={patternId} width={40} height={40} patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse">` containing
`<Line x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2={40} stroke={gridColor} strokeWidth="1" />` (vertical) and
`<Line x1="0" y1="0" x2={40} y2="0" stroke={gridColor} strokeWidth="1" />` (horizontal), filled onto
`<Rect width="100%" height="100%" fill={`url(#${patternId})`} />`. `patternId` comes from `useId()`.

Scan-line animation (GridBackground.tsx:45-69): `translateY` from `0` to `screenHeight`,
`withTiming({ duration: 8000, easing: Easing.linear })`, `withRepeat(-1, false)` — infinite, no
reverse; explicitly reset to `0` on each activation and `cancelAnimation` on cleanup.

Styles, verbatim (GridBackground.tsx:136-162):

```ts
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: {
    flex: 1,
    position: 'relative',
  },
  gridContainer: {
    ...StyleSheet.absoluteFillObject,
    zIndex: 0,
  },
  scanLine: {
    position: 'absolute',
    top: 0,
    left: 0,
    right: 0,
    height: 2,
    zIndex: 1,
    // Colour + glow come from `scanLineTint` above; only the geometry is static.
    shadowOffset: { width: 0, height: 0 },
    shadowOpacity: 0.8,
    shadowRadius: 10,
    elevation: 2,
  },
  content: {
    flex: 1,
    zIndex: 2,
  },
})
```

**z-index stack: grid `0` → scan line `1` → content `2`.** Scan line is `height: 2`, full width, glow
via `shadowRadius: 10` / `shadowOpacity: 0.8` / `elevation: 2`.

testIDs: `grid-raster-layer` (the SVG wrapper) and `grid-scan-line`.

**What it replaced**

- A private `GRID_COLORS` table that had drifted from the palette:
  ```ts
  dark:  { subtle: 'rgba(153, 186, 221, 0.05)', normal: 'rgba(153, 186, 221, 0.08)', strong: 'rgba(153, 186, 221, 0.15)' }
  light: { subtle: 'rgba(30, 58, 95, 0.06)',    normal: 'rgba(30, 58, 95, 0.10)',    strong: 'rgba(30, 58, 95, 0.18)' }
  ```
  Note the light base was **rgb(30,58,95)** while `light.primary` is **rgb(30,58,138)** — 43
  blue-points off (also recorded at `Colors.ts:50-51`). Dark subtle/normal moved **0.05→0.11** and
  **0.08→0.14**, strong **0.15→0.20**. Light values are numerically the same alphas on the corrected
  hue.
- The scan line was a hardcoded pre-recolor teal: `backgroundColor: 'rgba(78, 205, 196, 0.3)'` and
  `shadowColor: '#4ecdc4'`, both baked into the static `scanLine` rule. GridBackground.tsx:81-83:
  "a stranded pre-recolor teal (#4ecdc4) that never followed the badge-blue palette and read as a
  foreign green streak over the white light theme."
- The 30-line `getGridColor()` function with a `colorScheme === 'dark'` branch and an
  `as unknown as { grid?: string; gridLight?: string }` cast collapsed to the 5-line lookup.
- `shouldRasterizeIOS` / `renderToHardwareTextureAndroid` were `true` unconditionally → now
  `showScanLine`.
- The scan-line effect had **no cleanup** (no `cancelAnimation`) and did not reset to `0`.

**Consumers / mount points:** `Screen.tsx:200` (when `showGrid`), `LockScreen.tsx:118`
(`<GridBackground showScanLine={false}>`), plus the modals that host `ModalHeader`.

**Notes:** GridBackground.tsx:95-102 quantifies the rasterization change: "on a static grid it just
pins a full-screen texture per mounted GridBackground (~14 mounted at steady state — 4 eager tabs +
~10 drawer form screens). Android hardware layers are the expensive case."

  (`ICON_SIZE - 8`).
- `statusArea` — `marginTop 56`, centred, `minHeight 100`; `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"`.
- `statusText` / `dotsText` — **26px**, `letterSpacing 7`; dots have `minWidth: 70`,
  `textAlign: 'left'`, cycling `' '` / `' .'` / `' . .'` / `' . . .'` every **400ms**.
- `retryHintText` — **20px**, `letterSpacing 5`, **`opacity: 0.75`**.
- `subLabelText` — **18px**, `letterSpacing 5`.

Animations (all `useNativeDriver: true`):

| Animation | Values | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Header flicker (always on) | `1 → 0.55 → 1 → 0.7 → 1` | `7200 / 80 / 160 / 80 / 480` ms, looped (~8s cycle) — BiometricScannerHUD.tsx:226-254 |
| Frame breathing (scanning only) | opacity `1 ↔ 0.75` | `2500/2 = 1250` ms each leg, `Easing.inOut(Easing.ease)`, looped |
| Scan-line sweep (initializing + scanning) | `translateY` `50.4` (`round(280*0.18)`) → `280`, then instant reset | `2000` ms, `Easing.inOut(Easing.ease)`, looped |
| Icon pulse (scanning only) | opacity `1 ↔ 0.8`, scale `1 ↔ 1.02` | `3000/2 = 1500` ms each leg, `Easing.inOut(Easing.ease)`, looped |
| Retry hint fade-in-up | opacity `0→1`, translateY `10→0` | `400` ms, after a `600` ms delay |
| Authorized sub-label fade-in-up | opacity `0→1`, translateY `10→0` | **`300` ms** (hardcoded, not the shared constant) |

`testID="scanner-frame"` on the `Pressable` (pressable only when `failed`; `accessibilityRole` flips
`'image'` → `'button'`).

**What it replaced:** one line. `{isAuthorized && <AuthorizedSubLabel color="rgba(48,209,88,0.4)" />}`
→ `{isAuthorized && <AuthorizedSubLabel color={SCANNER_COLORS.authorized.text} />}`
(BiometricScannerHUD.tsx:520). Everything else in the diff is prettier reflow.

**Consumers / mount points:** `AuthenticatedSplashScreen.tsx:277-283` and `LockScreen.tsx:120-124`.

**Notes:** BiometricScannerHUD.tsx:516-519, quoted: "The state's own `text`, not a 40%-alpha green
typed inline. At 18px normal weight the literal measured **2.30:1** on this ground, against AA's
**4.5**; the token measures **7.29**. It was also the only colour literal left in this file."

```ts

scanning:     { primary: '#2B8CC1', glow: 'rgba(43,140,193,0.35)', text: 'rgba(153,186,221,0.9)' },
failed:       { primary: '#FF453A', glow: 'rgba(255,69,58,0.3)',   text: 'rgba(255,140,135,0.9)' },
```

Concretely: `failed.primary` **`#FF453A` → `#ff4757`**; `authorized.primary` **`#30D158` → `#10d177`**;
`failed.text` **`rgba(255,140,135,0.9)` → `#f0f4f8`**; `authorized.text` **`rgba(48,209,88,0.95)` →
`#10d177`**; the two `text` values for initializing/scanning lose their 0.9 alpha
(`rgba(153,186,221,0.9)` → flat `#99badd`); `initializing`/`scanning.primary` are unchanged in value,
only in provenance. Every dimension, timing, string and type/spacing constant is byte-identical.

**Consumers / mount points:** `BiometricScannerHUD.tsx:23-64` (the whole import block).

**Notes** (all in-file, quoting the contrast numbers verbatim):
- scanner-hud-constants.ts:8-14 — **ruling D6**: "ALWAYS DARK … Both hosts … paint
  `Colors.dark.background` full-bleed before the app theme is user-visible, so this palette is pinned
  to `Colors.dark` rather than following the active scheme. Pinned is not the same as invented …
  the three iOS system colours this file used to carry (`#FF453A`, `#30D158`, and `#2B8CC1` retyped as
  a literal) were a palette generation adrift from the app's own status tokens."
- scanner-hud-constants.ts:41-44 — measured on `Colors.dark.background`:
  `primary  info 3.94   error 4.40   success 7.29   (was 3.94/4.32/7.27)` and
  `text  failed 3.60 -> 8.03   authorized 6.70 -> 7.29`.
- scanner-hud-constants.ts:46-54 — why `failed.text` stops being red: at 20px normal weight under
  `opacity 0.75`, "the current soft red measures **3.60** and a flat `error` would be WORSE at
  **2.85**; there is no red on this navy that clears 4.5 through that opacity." It takes
  `errorOnLight`, the **D8(a)** foreground for the error severity, while the severity keeps being
  carried by the frame, brackets, glow and the 26px "AUTH FAILED" line.
- scanner-hud-constants.ts:166-179 — the type and spacing scales are **deliberately NOT** tokenised:
  "these are a bespoke scale for a 280px scanner frame … Only half of them have an exact token
  (20 = `xl`, 18 = `lg`, 48 = `xxl`, 20 = `mdlg`, 16 = `md`); 26, 56, 28 and 100 have none, and a
  half-mapped scale is worse than an unmapped one."

### `RootLayout` — `app/_layout.tsx`

**Status:** CHANGED
**Phase/PR:** `69229aaa fix(error): read the boot screens' palette from Colors.dark instead of
inventing one` (PR #123) · `98de5973 fix(theme): move the boot navy onto Colors.dark.background at all
six sites (D5a)` (PR #120) · `f6616df2 fix(routes): attribute a failed Mapbox SDK init` (PR #108) ·
`d1739700` prettier · `2f086078 style(lint)` (PR #105).

**Role:** The root Expo Router layout — Sentry init, Mapbox token registration, the boot state machine
(splash → init-failure → loading → app), and the themed navigation shell.

**Canonical recipe NOW — the visual surfaces**

`ThemedNavigationShell` (app/_layout.tsx:114-143) — three paint layers:

```tsx
const navigationTheme = useMemo(() => {
  const base = colorScheme === 'dark' ? NavDarkTheme : NavDefaultTheme
  return { ...base, colors: { ...base.colors, background: colors.background } }
}, [colorScheme, colors.background])

<NavigationThemeProvider value={navigationTheme}>
  <View style={{ flex: 1, backgroundColor: colors.background }}>
    <Stack
      screenOptions={{
        headerShown: false,
        contentStyle: { backgroundColor: colors.background },
      }}
    >
      <Stack.Screen name="(tabs)" />
      <Stack.Screen name="(form)" />
    </Stack>
  </View>
</NavigationThemeProvider>
```

Loading fallback (app/_layout.tsx:256-281):

```tsx
<View
  style={{
    flex: 1,
    justifyContent: 'center',
    alignItems: 'center',
    backgroundColor: Colors.dark.background,      // '#002853'
  }}
>
  <ActivityIndicator size="large" color={Colors.dark.primary} />   // '#2B8CC1'
</View>
```

Provider stack for the app branch (app/_layout.tsx:283-301):
`GestureHandlerRootView(flex:1)` → `ErrorBoundary` → `SafeAreaProvider` → `ThemeProvider` →
`KeyboardProvider statusBarTranslucent navigationBarTranslucent` → `AuthenticationProvider skipInitialAuth`
→ `[AppStateHandler, SyncBootstrap, DrizzleStudioDev(dev only), ThemedNavigationShell, Toast]`.

Boot branch order — **splash first, then init-failure, then loading, then app** (`_layout.tsx:227`,
`:244`, `:256`, `:283`). Splash and init-failure branches wrap only
`GestureHandlerRootView` + `SafeAreaProvider` (no `ThemeProvider`).

**What it replaced:** the loading fallback's `backgroundColor` was the literal `'#000314'` and the
spinner colour was the iOS system blue `'#007AFF'`. `_layout.tsx:271-277` records the swap: "This is
the literal's LAST live site in the app; its twin in `InitFailureScreen` moves in the same commit so
the boot sequence needs one verification pass, not two (**DEF-UI-021**). **3.66 -> 3.94** on this
ground, a non-text indicator against 1.4.11's 3:1."

**Consumers / mount points:** the app root.

**Notes:** `_layout.tsx:86-113` documents the three-JS-layer + one-native-layer paint fix for the
white wedges react-native-screens exposes at the display corners during stack transitions: the wrapper
`View` is "the layer the rounded corners actually reveal; painting it is what removes the white. (nav
theme + contentStyle alone do NOT fix it: they paint the screens themselves, and the screens are the
thing being corner-rounded — the exposure is BEHIND them.)" The fourth belt is a root-level
`backgroundColor` (`Colors.dark.background`) in `app.config.js`, per **ruling D5(a)**.

### `TabsLayout` — `app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx`

**Status:** CHANGED
**Phase/PR:** `ad62ecb2 refactor(design-system): route raw spacing through Layout.spacing, delete the
arithmetic` (PR #124) · `16b2ae98 perf(tabs): freeze blurred tabs [P3]` (PR #94) · `d1739700` prettier.

**Role:** The four-tab bottom navigator.

**Canonical recipe NOW** — the whole `screenOptions` visual block (`(tabs)/_layout.tsx:11-38`):

```tsx
screenOptions={{
  headerShown: false,
  tabBarActiveTintColor: colors.primary,
  tabBarInactiveTintColor: colors.textSecondary,
  tabBarStyle: {
    backgroundColor: colors.card,
    borderTopColor: colors.border,
    paddingTop: Layout.spacing.xsm,
  },
  lazy: false,
  freezeOnBlur: true,
}}
```

**Resolved tab-bar chrome:**

| | light | dark |
|---|---|---|
| `tabBarActiveTintColor` (`colors.primary`) | `#1e3a8a` | `#2B8CC1` |
| `tabBarInactiveTintColor` (`colors.textSecondary`) | `#4b5563` | `#99badd` |
| `tabBarStyle.backgroundColor` (`colors.card`) | `#ffffff` | `#0e3965` |
| `tabBarStyle.borderTopColor` (`colors.border`) | `#e5e7eb` | `#1c4e84` |
| `tabBarStyle.paddingTop` (`Layout.spacing.xsm`) | `6` | `6` |

**HEIGHT IS NOT SET.** There is no `height` key anywhere in `tabBarStyle` — the bar takes
`@react-navigation/bottom-tabs`' platform default plus the safe-area inset, plus the `6` of
`paddingTop`. The only explicit vertical value in the whole file is that `paddingTop: 6`. There is
also no `tabBarLabelStyle`, no `tabBarIconStyle`, no `tabBarItemStyle` and no `borderTopWidth`
override (RN's default hairline applies).

**Tabs, in mounted order** (`(tabs)/_layout.tsx:40-73`) — every icon takes the navigator-supplied
`size` and `color`, so icon size follows the library default (24 on both platforms) and the colour is
the active/inactive tint above:

| order | route | `title` | icon |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `home` | `Dashboard` | `desktop-outline` |
| 2 | `cases` | `Cases` | `folder` |
| 3 | `map` | `Map` | `map` |
| 4 | `export` | `Export` | `archive-outline` |

**What it replaced:** `paddingTop: 6` was a raw literal (now `Layout.spacing.xsm`, same value), and
`freezeOnBlur: true` is new. Colours, icons, titles and order are unchanged from baseline. There was
no `height` at baseline either.

**Consumers / mount points:** `app/_layout.tsx:137` (`<Stack.Screen name="(tabs)" />`).

**Notes:**
- `(tabs)/_layout.tsx:20-26` — `lazy: false` is safe despite the Map tab, because "its actual mount is
  gated inside `app/(tabs)/map.tsx`: the picker shell renders eagerly while `<MapHost>` only mounts
  after the user picks a case."
- `(tabs)/_layout.tsx:28-36` — `freezeOnBlur: true` pairs with `lazy: false` rather than replacing it:
  "first render stays eager, blurred re-renders stop … native views stay alive, so the Mapbox GL
  surface on the Map tab persists across freeze/unfreeze. [Optimization review P3]"
- `(tabs)/_layout.tsx:67-68` — the Export icon is explicitly **interim**: "reads as 'evidence
  package'; final icon is design-prompt territory (architecture §7)."

`d1739700` prettier.

**Role:** The launch experience — a static door-frame poster, an always-mounted preloading splash
video, and the `BiometricScannerHUD` overlaid during the auth phase, ending in a fade to the app.

**Canonical recipe NOW**

Scrim knobs (AuthenticatedSplashScreen.tsx:305-307):

```ts
const HUD_SCRIM_TINT = '0, 0, 0'
const HUD_SCRIM_OPACITY = 0.4
const HUD_SCRIM = `rgba(${HUD_SCRIM_TINT}, ${HUD_SCRIM_OPACITY})`
```
→ **`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4)`**.

Styles, verbatim (AuthenticatedSplashScreen.tsx:309-334):

```ts
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: {
    flex: 1,
    // Static dark: this covers the hand-off from the native splash, whose
    // colour lives in app.config.js. Ruling D5(a) moves both together.
    backgroundColor: Colors.dark.background,
    justifyContent: 'center',
    alignItems: 'center',
    overflow: 'hidden',
  },
  backgroundImage: {
    position: 'absolute',
  },
  video: {
    position: 'absolute',
  },
  authOverlay: {
    ...StyleSheet.absoluteFillObject,
    justifyContent: 'center',
    alignItems: 'center',
    // Tuned by eye - see HUD_SCRIM above for the two knobs and the history.
    // Deliberately NOT `Colors.dark.scrim`: this surface is pre-theme and its
    // ground is a video frame, so it does not want the app's navy sheet dim.
    backgroundColor: HUD_SCRIM,
  },
})
```

Resolved: container `backgroundColor: '#002853'`; `authOverlay` `backgroundColor: 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4)'`,
absolute-fill, centred.

Media sizing (AuthenticatedSplashScreen.tsx:25, 52-69) — cover-fit against a **720x1280 (0.5625)**
aspect ratio:

```ts
const VIDEO_ASPECT_RATIO = 720 / 1280   // 0.5625
// screenAspect > 0.5625 → { width: screenWidth,  height: screenWidth / 0.5625 }
// else                  → { width: screenHeight * 0.5625, height: screenHeight }
```
Both the poster (`assets/splash-video-frame1.png`, `resizeMode="cover"`) and the video
(`assets/splash-video.mp4`, `ResizeMode.COVER`) take those dimensions, both `position: 'absolute'`.

Timing (AuthenticatedSplashScreen.tsx:28-34):

```ts
const HOLD_DURATION_MS = 500        // hold after video ends before fading
const FADE_DURATION_MS = 300        // fade-to-app opacity 1 → 0
const AUTO_TRIGGER_DELAY_MS = 500   // delay before auto-firing the biometric prompt
```

Video props: `isLooping={false}`, `isMuted={true}`, `useNativeControls={false}`,
`progressUpdateIntervalMillis={500}`, `{...(Platform.OS === 'ios' && { ignoreSilentSwitch: 'ignore' })}`.
It is **always mounted** so it preloads during auth; the poster stays visible until
`onReadyForDisplay` fires (`phase === 'authenticating' || !isVideoReady`).

Phases: `'authenticating' | 'playing_video' | 'fading_out' | 'complete'`.

**What it replaced** — this one surface moved four times; the full ladder:

| Commit | `authOverlay.backgroundColor` |
|---|---|
| baseline `d9606460` | `'rgba(0, 3, 20, 0.75)'` (comment: "Dark scrim ensures HUD reads clearly over any background image") |
| `1b05e9d1` (PR #120) | `Colors.dark.scrim` → **`rgba(0, 40, 83, 0.32)`** at `main`, but **0.9 alpha navy** when that commit landed |
| `65cd5e99` (PR #127) | key **deleted** — no scrim at all |
| `11228638` (PR #127) | `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2)` on the two named knobs |
| `2688fdfd` (PR #127) | **`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4)`** ← current |

Container `backgroundColor` was the literal `'#000314'` at baseline → `Colors.dark.background`
(`#002853`) at `98de5973`, under **ruling D5(a)**.

**Consumers / mount points:** `app/_layout.tsx:26` (import via `@/features/biometrics`),
`app/_layout.tsx:231-234` (rendered when `showSplash`).

**Notes** — the three PR #127 splash commits, in their own words:
- `65cd5e99` removed the scrim entirely on the theory that the poster IS frame 1 of the video, so "the
  hand-off was designed to be invisible. The scrim was the only thing breaking it: it darkened the
  poster and then vanished at the cut, so the background jumped brighter at exactly the moment the
  video began." It also records the drift history: the overlay was `rgba(0, 3, 20, 0.75)`, the SAME
  `#000314` the container carried, so it barely registered; D5(a) moved the container to
  `Colors.dark.background`, the two stopped agreeing, and the repair pointed the overlay at the shared
  `scrim` token — which was **0.9 alpha**. "That is the 'much darker' the owner reported; it was a
  second-order campaign side effect, not a design decision." It explicitly ships **no unit test**,
  flagged rather than skipped quietly.
- `11228638` reversed that: "Removing it entirely was the wrong read on the owner's report. The
  off-putting part was the NAVY, not the presence of a scrim." Back at `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2)`,
  "started deliberately low to be walked up rather than down. For scale: the original was 0.75, and
  the repair that followed pointed it at the 0.9 navy token, so both previous values were far
  heavier." The two knobs are named constants sitting adjacent because it is tuned by eye on device;
  `'0, 40, 83'` is documented in-file as the navy alternative.
- `2688fdfd` settled it: "Device-approved. Landed at 0.2 to be walked up rather than down; **0.4** is
  where it reads right — the HUD is seated without the cold navy cast that made the 0.9 token version
  off-putting."
- AuthenticatedSplashScreen.tsx:329-331 — "Deliberately NOT `Colors.dark.scrim`: this surface is
  pre-theme and its ground is a video frame … a change to the sheet dim should never move the splash
  again."

### `LockScreen` — `src/features/biometrics/components/LockScreen.tsx`

**Status:** CHANGED (async containment only; **no visual change**)
**Phase/PR:** `fac02169 fix(biometrics): contain async rejections at the auth gate's void boundaries`
(PR #108) · `d1739700` prettier.

**Role:** The return-from-background lock overlay — the same `BiometricScannerHUD` on an opaque themed
ground with the grid but **no scan line**, auto-firing the biometric prompt on mount.

**Canonical recipe NOW** (LockScreen.tsx:116-141):

```tsx
<View style={[styles.container, { backgroundColor: colors.background }]} testID="lock-screen">
  <GridBackground showScanLine={false}>
    <SafeAreaView style={styles.overlay}>
      <BiometricScannerHUD
        scannerState={scannerState}
        biometricType={biometricType}
        onRetry={() => void handleAuthenticateWithGlobalLock()}
      />
    </SafeAreaView>
  </GridBackground>
</View>

const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: {
    // Use absoluteFill to ensure LockScreen covers the entire screen as an overlay.
    // This works with the overlay pattern in AuthenticationProvider to preserve
    // navigation state while fully obscuring the app content behind it.
    ...StyleSheet.absoluteFillObject,
  },
  overlay: {
    flex: 1,
  },
})
```

Resolved: `container` = `position:absolute; top/left/right/bottom: 0`, `backgroundColor:
colors.background` (light `#ffffff` / dark `#002853`) — **theme-following**, unlike the splash.
`GridBackground` takes its defaults (`gridSize 40`, `gridOpacity 'subtle'`) with `showScanLine={false}`.
**NO scrim** over the HUD — the ground is opaque.

Timing constants (LockScreen.tsx:24, 30): `AUTO_TRIGGER_DELAY_MS = 300`, `MIN_AUTH_INTERVAL_MS = 1000`.
Initial scanner state is `'scanning'` (LockScreen.tsx:69) — the splash starts at `'initializing'`.

**What it replaced:** nothing visually. `fac02169` only wrapped the two `handleAuthenticate` call
sites in `void …()` with the containment comments; the styles are byte-identical to baseline.

**Consumers / mount points:** `AuthenticationProvider` (overlay pattern).

**Notes:** LockScreen.tsx:36-41 — the module-level `globalAuthLock` survives remounts.
`65cd5e99`'s body cites this screen as the reference for the no-scrim splash decision: "Its sibling
`LockScreen` — the return-from-background HUD, which reads correctly today — already renders this same
`BiometricScannerHUD` with no scrim on an opaque ground."

Two CTAs, both `fullWidth`, both with icon+label children at `Layout.iconSize.sm` (**20px**):

**What it replaced**

- Two hand-rolled `Pressable`s with `style={({pressed}) => […, pressed && styles.buttonPressed]}`, and

  ```ts
  button: { flexDirection:'row', alignItems:'center', justifyContent:'center',
  ```

- `iconContainer.borderRadius` was the literal `60` → `Layout.borderRadius.full` (9999).
- `subtitle.lineHeight` was the literal `22` → `16 × 1.5 = 24`.
- `warningText.color` was **`colors.warning`**.

**Consumers / mount points:** `AuthenticationProvider`.

**Notes** (contrast numbers quoted verbatim):
- BiometricsUnavailableScreen.tsx:63-68 — the icon+label children mean the caller sets the label
  colour rather than `Button`'s string path; it "mirrors that path byte-for-byte with
  `colors.textInverse` (the **DEF-UI-018** precedent): measured on `Button`'s own primary gradient,
  `textInverse` is **5.01 / 3.34:1** dark against `onPrimary`'s **2.94 / 4.40:1**, and identical in
  light."
- BiometricsUnavailableScreen.tsx:98-101 — "`warningOnLight`, not `warning`: the saturated amber
  measures **2.15:1** on `colors.background` in light mode (**10.67:1** dark, correct in one theme
  only). `warningOnLight` measures **9.07:1 light / 13.30:1 dark** and keeps a warning hue in light."

| `title` | `#f0f4f8`, `20px`, `700`, centred, `marginBottom 16` |

Copy, verbatim:

- Variant A (`isDatabaseEncryptionUnavailableError`): title "This Build Cannot Protect Evidence";
  message "This copy of the app was built without database encryption (SQLCipher). Evidence stored by
  this build would NOT be encrypted at rest."; guidance "Do not use this build. Install a release
  build, or contact the developer — this is a build fault, not a problem with your data."
  **No Retry button.**
- Variant B (`isDatabaseEncryptionKeyError`): title "Database Cannot Be Decrypted"; message "The
  evidence database on this device cannot be decrypted — the encryption key is missing or incorrect.";
  guidance "If this device holds no evidence yet, deleting and reinstalling the app will start fresh.
  If it may hold real case data, do NOT delete the app — contact the developer first."
  **No Retry button.**
- Variant C (generic): title "App Failed to Start"; message = `error.message` (or `String(error)`);
  guidance "This may be temporary. If retrying does not help, restart the app — and if it persists,
  contact the developer."; **Retry button**, label "Retry",
  `testID="init-failure-retry"`, `accessibilityLabel="Retry initialization"`.

All three carry `testID="init-failure-screen"` and `accessibilityRole="header"` on the title.

**What it replaced**

```ts
scroll.backgroundColor:  '#000314'  → Colors.dark.background  (#002853)
container.paddingHorizontal: 32     → Layout.spacing.xl       (same 32)
container.paddingVertical:   48     → Layout.spacing.xxl      (same 48)
title.color:   '#FFFFFF'            → Colors.dark.text        (#f0f4f8)
title.fontSize: 20                  → Typography.fontSize.xl  (same 20)
title.fontWeight: '700'             → Typography.fontWeight.bold (same)
title.marginBottom: 16              → Layout.spacing.md       (same 16)
message.color: '#C7CBD6'            → Colors.dark.textSecondary (#99badd)
message.marginBottom: 12            → Layout.spacing.base     (same 12)
guidance.color: '#8A8F9C'           → Colors.dark.textTertiary (#7a9fc4)
retryButton.paddingVertical: 12     → Layout.spacing.base     (same 12)
retryButton.borderRadius: 10        → Layout.borderRadius.control (same 10)
retryButton.backgroundColor: '#007AFF' → Colors.dark.primaryDark (#1F6B99)
retryButton: minHeight + justifyContent: 'center'  ← BOTH NEW
retryLabel.color: '#FFFFFF'         → Colors.dark.onPrimary   (#ffffff, same)
retryLabel.fontSize: 16             → Typography.fontSize.base (same 16)
retryLabel.fontWeight: '600'        → Typography.fontWeight.semibold (same)
```

`message.fontSize: 15` / `lineHeight: 22`, `guidance.fontSize: 13` / `lineHeight: 20`,
`retryButton.marginTop: 28` and `paddingHorizontal: 40` are **unchanged raw literals** — they have no
token.

**Consumers / mount points:** `app/_layout.tsx:17` (import), `app/_layout.tsx:248` (rendered when
`initError !== null`, before the `!isInitialized` spinner branch).

**Notes** — InitFailureScreen.tsx:23-41, quoted in full because it carries the contrast ledger:

> Static does NOT mean hand-mixed. Every colour below reads `Colors.dark` directly, because a screen
> that cannot call `useTheme()` is still part of the app's palette; the greys it used to carry
> (`#C7CBD6`, `#8A8F9C`) and the `#007AFF` iOS system blue were an invented iOS look sitting on the
> app's own navy. Measured on `Colors.dark.background`:
>
> ```
> title     #FFFFFF 14.70 -> `text`           13.30
> message   #C7CBD6  9.06 -> `textSecondary`   7.30
> guidance  #8A8F9C  4.54 -> `textTertiary`    5.31
> retry     #FFFFFF on #007AFF 4.02 -> `onPrimary` on `primaryDark` 5.80
> ```
>
> The retry button fills `primaryDark`, not `primary`: `onPrimary` on the flat `primary` the plan's
> row names measures **3.73:1** (**DEF-UI-001**), which would have traded one failure for another on
> the one control this screen offers.

Also InitFailureScreen.tsx:9-21 — the two typed encryption failures are discriminated because "their
remedies are OPPOSITE, and getting them backwards destroys evidence"; neither offers a Retry.
The `flexGrow` (not `flex`) choice is attributed to **PR #81 L1**.

### `RouteErrorFallback` — `src/components/error/RouteErrorFallback.tsx`

**Status:** NEW since baseline (file does not exist at `d9606460`)
**Phase/PR:** `93b7585d refactor(error): extract one RouteErrorFallback for the four wizard routes`
(PR #115), pinned by `bfcb27e5 test(error): pin RouteErrorFallback's contract, including the logError
it carries`.

**Role:** The `ErrorBoundary` fallback body for a wizard route — a centred "Something went wrong"
title, the caller's copy, and a "Go Back" `Button`. It also owns the `logError` call.

**Canonical recipe NOW** (RouteErrorFallback.tsx:50-81):

```tsx
<View style={[styles.errorContainer, { backgroundColor: colors.background }]} testID={testID}>
  <Text style={[styles.errorTitle, { color: colors.text }]}>Something went wrong</Text>
  <Text style={[styles.errorMessage, { color: colors.textSecondary }]}>{message}</Text>
  <Button onPress={onGoBack} style={styles.errorButton}>
    Go Back
  </Button>
</View>

const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  errorContainer: {
    flex: 1,
    justifyContent: 'center',
    alignItems: 'center',
    padding: Layout.spacing.xl,
  },
  errorTitle: {
    fontSize: Typography.fontSize.xl,
    fontWeight: Typography.fontWeight.bold,
    marginBottom: Layout.spacing.md,
  },
  errorMessage: {
    fontSize: Typography.fontSize.base,
    textAlign: 'center',
    marginBottom: Layout.spacing.lg,
  },
  errorButton: {
    marginTop: Layout.spacing.md,
  },
})
```

Resolved: container `flex 1 / centred / padding 32` on `colors.background`. Title `20px / 700 /
marginBottom 16` on `colors.text` — **note: `xl`(20), not `2xl`(24)**, and it is NOT centred
(`textAlign` is unset). Message `16px / centred / marginBottom 24` on `colors.textSecondary`. Button
gets only `marginTop 16`; it is NOT `fullWidth`.

Props: `error` (logged here, only `message` ever shown), `context` (log tag), `message` (the copy —
a plain string, not a fallback), `onGoBack`, `testID?`.

**What it replaced:** four byte-identical inline copies plus four byte-identical four-rule StyleSheet
blocks, in `app/(form)/notes.tsx`, `ocr-capture.tsx`, `media-capture.tsx`, `audio-recording.tsx`.
"They differed only in the copy shown and in what 'go back' means, so only those two are props"
(RouteErrorFallback.tsx:5-10).

**Consumers / mount points:**

- `app/(form)/notes.tsx:24, 305`
- `app/(form)/ocr-capture.tsx:12, 414`
- `app/(form)/media-capture.tsx:26, 259`
- `app/(form)/audio-recording.tsx:26, 254`

**Notes:** RouteErrorFallback.tsx:11-14 — "Logging lives here rather than in the callers: three of the
four copies called `logError` and one (ocr-capture) silently did not, so an OCR crash showed the user
a screen and told nobody. Passing `context` makes that impossible to forget." RouteErrorFallback.tsx:30-32 —
"Callers decide whether `error.message` is fit to surface; audio-recording deliberately never shows the
raw library text."

## 2.C Map view (PR #118 Phase 1 + PR #127 redesign)

### Map-view README — the binding redesign rules

**File:** `src/features/location/map-view/README.md` (418 lines at `main`)
**Status:** CHANGED (98 lines touched)
**Phase/PR:** `80f0ea0d`→ actually `80ddaa6a docs(map-view): update README for the redesigned map chrome` (PR #127), plus prettier reflow from `d1739700`.

**IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF.** The recon brief said the README is "the redesign's own design record" carrying rules like *"all four sides, drop the left accent bar"*, CTA sizing, and an *"always-dark floating-chrome rule"*. **None of those three rules is in the README.** I grepped it for `accent`, `four sides`, `CTA`, `always-dark`, `D3`, `contrast`, `DEF-` and the only hit of substance is line 261. The README is an architecture/API document; the redesign's binding visual rulings live in **commit messages** (`7df5148b`, `e882912f`) and in **in-file docblocks**. Downstream: do not go looking for a design record in this README that does not exist — the rules below are quoted from where they actually live.

**Role:** Architecture + public-API document for the `map-view` sub-feature; it describes what each component is for, the hook contracts, the services, and the theming ruling — not a token sheet.

#### Binding rule 1 — the floating map chrome is NO LONGER always-dark (D3(a) SUPERSEDED)

Verbatim, `README.md:261`:

> `@/context/ThemeContext` — `useTheme()`. The **sheet** (`MapBottomSheet`, `SheetBackground`, `SheetHandle`, `LocationList`, `LocationRow`, `LocationDetailCard`) and the **filters modal** (`MapFiltersSheet`) read it directly: they are app chrome and follow the app theme (ruling D3a). The **floating chrome** over the tiles (`MapControls`, `MapScaleBar`) is also theme-aware — per the 2026-08 chrome-redesign ruling the whole map view follows the app theme (a light sheet under dark floating chrome read as two different apps) — but receives `isDark` as a prop instead of reading context, so it stays context-free and testable in isolation. Its light glass variants are near-opaque (see `MAP_GLASS_COLORS`) because translucent white over satellite tiles is illegible. Only elements painted **onto** the tiles (pins, clusters, the proximity ring, camera markers) remain theme-invariant.

The same ruling is restated in `MapControls.tsx:23-28`:

> Theme awareness: the whole map view follows the app theme (owner ruling superseding the always-dark reading of D3a — a light bottom sheet under dark floating chrome read as two different apps). `isDark` arrives as a prop (not from context) to keep the component context-free and trivially testable; MAP_GLASS_COLORS provides near-opaque light variants because translucent white over busy satellite imagery is illegible.

**So the answer to "is floating chrome always-dark?" is NO, not any more.** What IS still theme-invariant (always painted from `Colors.dark` / fixed values regardless of app theme):
- `PIN_COLORS` (location + incident pins) — `constants/index.ts:58-67`
- `CLUSTER_CIRCLE_STYLE` + `CIRCLE_LAYER_STYLE` — `constants/index.ts:198-229`
- `PROXIMITY_COLORS` (ring fill + line) — `constants/index.ts:77-84`
- `CAMERA_MARKER` (white base, near-black glyph, navy callout) — `constants/index.ts:120-140`
- `MAP_SURFACE_COLORS` (error overlay, callout bubbles) — `constants/index.ts:92-109`
- `CaseMapView`'s cold-start `loadingCover` — `CaseMapView.tsx:902-905`
- `MapHost`'s error overlay + retry button — `MapHost.tsx:580-610`

#### Binding rule 2 — card borders on all four sides, the left accent bar is DROPPED

NOT in the README. It is commit `7df5148b style(map): draw card borders on all four sides, drop the left accent bar` (2026-08-24). Message verbatim:

> Both surfaces used the same idiom: `borderWidth: 1` with `borderLeftWidth: 4`, the left edge painted `transparent` when unselected and tinted when selected. The reserved edge was meant to stop selection reflowing the row - but it also meant every UNSELECTED card rendered a 4px transparent gap where its left border should be, so the border read as missing on three sides out of four. Selected cards wore a heavy bar down one side.
>
> `LocationRow` (map sheet): uniform 1px `glass.border`, and selection is no longer indicated at all. Tapping a row opens that location's own sheet, which is the signal - the border does not need to carry it. `statusColor` is no longer threaded into the shell; the status dot still uses it.
>
> `MapPicker` (case picker): uniform border, selection carried evenly by weight and colour - 2px `primary` against 1px glass. The 1px difference reflows the row by 1px on selection, versus the 3px reflow the reserved edge existed to prevent.
>
> The drawer keeps its 4px left accent. That one is owner-approved and reads correctly against a full-height nav surface; these are cards in a list.

Two surfaces, **two different outcomes** — see the `LocationRow` and `MapPicker` sections below.

#### Binding rule 3 — map-view CTAs drop to the app-default `medium` size

NOT in the README. Commit `e882912f style(map): size the map-view CTAs like every other primary in the app` (2026-08-24). Message verbatim:

> Counted across the app: **124** `<Button>` use the default `medium`, 12 use `small`, 1 is explicitly `medium`, and exactly **3** use `size="large"`. All three were in map-view: Export Map, Edit Incident Location, and Go to Location. That is a feature-local convention, not an app one.
>
> `size="large"` is `paddingVertical: xl` on `touchTarget.large` (56); the default `medium` is `md` on `touchTarget.comfortable` (48). The closest analogue in the app is the wizard's full-width Next CTA, which takes the default. All three now do too.
>
> NOT changed: `Layout.borderRadius.control` (10) against the cards' `lg` (12). That 2pt difference is an app-wide design-system distinction between controls and surfaces - every one of the 137 buttons reads it. Changing it to match one screen's cards would be a global change made for a local reason.

Resolved values from `src/components/common/Button.tsx:96-111` and `:181-189`:

| size | paddingHorizontal | paddingVertical | minHeight | fontSize |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `small` | `Layout.spacing.md` = 16 | `Layout.spacing.sm` = 8 | `Layout.touchTarget.min` = 44 | `Typography.fontSize.sm` = 14 |
| `medium` (default, **now used**) | `Layout.spacing.lg` = 24 | `Layout.spacing.md` = 16 | `Layout.touchTarget.comfortable` = 48 | `Typography.fontSize.base` = 16 |
| `large` (**removed from map-view**) | `Layout.spacing.xl` = 32 | `Layout.spacing.lg` = 24 | `Layout.touchTarget.large` = 56 | `Typography.fontSize.lg` = 18 |

All `Button`s carry `borderRadius: Layout.borderRadius.control` = **10** and `borderWidth: 1` (`Button.tsx:90-91`).

#### Other README facts worth porting

- Sheet detents named at `README.md:304`: "Three snap points — `peek` (88pt), `partial` (40%), `full` (65%) — indexed PEEK(0) / PARTIAL(1) / FULL(2)."
- `README.md:274` (workflow) — the new filter split: *"`MapControls` emits `setSearchText` from the search field; `MapFiltersSheet` (opened from the search chrome's filter button) emits `setStatusFilter`, the proximity toggle, and radius changes… The filter button's badge counts active statuses + an active proximity ring (never the search text, which is visible in the field), and the sheet's Clear All resets filters and deactivates proximity in one tap."*
- `README.md:300` — *"While the ring is active, `MapControls` shows a compact summary chip ("2 km · 5 of 9") whose ✕ deactivates and whose body re-opens the filters sheet."*
- `README.md:407` — the opaque-sheet performance rule: *"`SHEET_SURFACE_COLORS[scheme].backgroundGradient` is fully opaque in **both** themes so the compositor can occlude the live Mapbox GL surface behind the sheet during drags (a translucent surface dropped the drag to ~45fps). This is why the sheet does not use `GlassColors[scheme].sheet`, whose dark gradient starts at 0.98 alpha."*
- `README.md:259` — the filters modal deliberately uses `@/components/common/GlassBottomSheet` + `Button` + `Switch`, *"deliberately NOT `@gorhom/bottom-sheet`, which stays scoped to the draggable locations sheet"*.
- ASCII component map, `README.md:23-24`:
  - `MapControls.tsx  # Floating single-row search chrome: back/close, search field, filter button, proximity chip`
  - `MapFiltersSheet.tsx  # GlassBottomSheet modal: status filters, proximity toggle + radius presets, Clear All`

**Camera geometry constants** (these matter for demo camera parity), `MapHost.tsx:196-231`:

```js
const { height: screenHeight } = useWindowDimensions()
const detailSheetHeightPx = screenHeight * 0.65
const TAP_FLY_PADDING_TOP = insets.top + 120
const TAP_FLY_MIN_ZOOM = 18

```

Both top paddings were **reduced by the chrome collapse**. `MapHost.tsx:205-206`:
> 120 = ~60pt chrome (single search row, plus the proximity chip when active) + ~60pt of eye-line push. **Down from 170 when the chrome was three rows of pills.**

`MapHost.tsx:223-226`:
> Top: insets.top + 110pt (single-row search chrome + proximity chip allowance + breathing room) — keeps the northernmost pin clear of the search bar. **Down from 180 when the chrome was three rows of pills.**

**Filter badge count derivation** — `MapHost.tsx:266-268`:
```js
// Filter button badge: active status filters + one for an active proximity
// ring. Search text is deliberately excluded — it is visible in the field.
const filterBadgeCount = (filters.statuses?.length ?? 0) + (proximityIsActive ? 1 : 0)
```
Note `useMapFilter().activeFilterCount` is deliberately NOT consumed (`MapHost.tsx:111-114`).

**Filters-sheet visibility is host-owned** — `MapHost.tsx:163-167`:
```js
const [filtersVisible, setFiltersVisible] = useState(false)
const handleOpenFilters = useCallback(() => setFiltersVisible(true), [])
const handleCloseFilters = useCallback(() => setFiltersVisible(false), [])
```

**Clear All composition** — `MapHost.tsx:415-423`: `clearFilters()` then `proximityDeactivate()` if active.

**Counts** — `MapHost.tsx:238-244`:
```js
const proximityActiveResult = proximityIsActive ? proximityResult : null
const locationCount =
  filteredCollection?.features.filter((f) => f.properties?.featureType === 'location').length ?? 0
const displayCollection = proximityActiveResult?.filteredCollection ?? filteredCollection
const proximityRing = proximityActiveResult?.radiusPolygon ?? null
const filteredCount = proximityActiveResult?.locationCount ?? locationCount
```

**Props passed to `MapControls`** (`:505-521`): `filters`, `onSearchChange=setSearchText`, `onOpenFilters`, `filterBadgeCount`, `onClose=onChangeCaseRequest`, `proximityActive`, `proximityRadius`, `onProximityDeactivate`, `locationCount`, `filteredCount`, `isDark`, `safeAreaTop=insets.top`.

**What it replaced.** At baseline `MapHost` rendered:
- a `MapControls` with the full three-row API (`onStatusToggle`, `onClearFilters`, `activeFilterCount`, `onProximityToggle`, `onRadiusChange`)
- **no** `MapFiltersSheet`
- an **absolutely-positioned "Change Case" pill** of its own, which `MapControls.tsx:11-13` records as removed:
  > The close button replaces MapHost's absolutely-positioned "Change Case" pill (which used a different colour system and could overlap the count badge). Rendered only when `onClose` is provided — the same gating the pill had on `onChangeCaseRequest`.
- a full-screen "Loading locations…" overlay (deleted; see `:540-543`)
- a non-theme-aware `container` (always-dark) — now `{ backgroundColor: colors.background }`
- `TAP_FLY_PADDING_TOP = insets.top + 170`, `INITIAL_FIT_PADDING_TOP = insets.top + 180`

**Notes.** `MapHost.tsx:574-576` carries a **now-stale comment** — it still says "the always-dark chrome below (error overlay, retry, **Change Case pill**)". The Change Case pill no longer exists in this file; the error overlay and retry do and are still always-dark. Flag for the demo port: don't reintroduce a pill.

**Notes.** `constants/index.ts:148-162` on the FPS value:
> Mapbox's default is *adaptive* — it picks a rate it judges the device can sustain, which on this app settles at 60 even on a 120Hz panel… Two things outrank this value, so do not read a 60 on the perf monitor as proof it did nothing: iOS caps the whole app at 60Hz unless Info.plist carries `CADisableMinimumFrameDuration` (not set by this repo's config); iOS drops ProMotion to 60Hz under thermal pressure or Low Power Mode… Android treats it as a ceiling bounded by the hardware.

Not portable to a web demo — record it and move on.
