### `MapControls` — `src/features/location/map-view/components/MapControls.tsx`

**Status:** CHANGED — effectively **rewritten** (529 lines touched; 442-line baseline → 357-line current)
**Phase/PR:** `eb261c52` + `a1f6c195` (PR #118 Phase 1), then `1740f226 feat(map-view): collapse the floating map chrome into a single-row search bar` and `ae5a17ab fix(icons): restore the subpath import in MapControls, and guard it (H1)` (PR #127).

**Role:** The floating chrome over the tiles. Now exactly two rows: a search row (`[← close] [🔍 search … ✕ | filters ●]`) and, only while proximity is active, a summary chip.

#### D3(a) always-dark: HOW IT IS ACTUALLY IMPLEMENTED

**There is no `ForceColorScheme` wrapper and no hardcoded dark palette.** The component is fully theme-aware and takes `isDark` as a **prop**. `MapControls.tsx:69-73`:
```ts
  /**
   * True when the app is in dark mode (from useTheme().isDark). Passed as a
   * prop rather than read from context so the component stays context-free.
   */
  isDark: boolean
```
`MapHost.tsx:519` passes `isDark={isDark}` straight from `useTheme()`.

#### DEF-UI-015 / DEF-062 — what the file says

**Nothing.** `MapControls.tsx` contains no `DEF-` reference, no contrast ratio, and no mention of 1.12:1. The whole deferral history lives in docs. The current state, `docs/code-reviews/deferred-items.md:695-698` VERBATIM:

> **CLOSED 2026-08-24 by owner ruling — accepted as a deliberate design choice, NOT fixed.** The map chrome was redesigned on `claude/mapview-chrome-redesign-p8v1wp` (single-row search bar + `MapFiltersSheet`), and the owner ruled the resulting pill treatment final: *"this was a deliberate design choice that we made when redesigning so that deferral is no longer relevant."*
>
> **What that accepts, stated plainly so it is not lost:** the measured shortfall this row was opened for is not disputed and has not been re-measured as resolved. The pills were recorded at **1.70:1** over dark satellite tiles against WCAG AA, and this closure is an explicit decision to ship that, not evidence it improved. Recorded this way because a contrast row closed on preference reads identically to one closed on a fix unless the difference is written down.
>
> **Reopen trigger:** none. This row does not re-arm on a future edit to `MAP_GLASS_COLORS` or `MapControls.tsx` — its trigger fired during this very redesign and the ruling was made with the new chrome in hand. A future accessibility pass that revisits map legibility should open a NEW row rather than resurrect this one.

The original measurements, `deferred-items.md:703` VERBATIM:

> light pill `rgba(255,255,255,0.60)` under secondary text `#6b7280` measures 4.83 / 4.10 / 2.49 / **1.70:1** across bright / pale-sand / vegetation / dark tiles, and the count badge `#9ca3af` measures 2.54 / 2.15 / 1.31 / **1.12:1**; the dark pill over a bright tile gives 4.43 / 2.43 / **1.77:1**. All twelve cells were independently recomputed by the campaign aggregator and reproduce exactly.

**The 1.12:1 cell no longer has a subject.** It was the *count badge* text on `colors.textTertiary` in the old row-1 count pill — **that pill was deleted** by the chrome collapse. The 1.70:1 cell had its ground raised from `rgba(255,255,255,0.60)` to `rgba(255,255,255,0.92)` and its foreground was `textSecondary` `#6b7280` → now `#4b5563` (`Colors.light.textSecondary`). Neither was re-measured; the row was closed on preference.

`MAP_GLASS_COLORS.containerBgLight`'s own docblock, `constants/index.ts:258-266` VERBATIM:

### The collapsed map search bar — `MapControls.tsx:112-188`

**Status:** NEW since baseline (in the sense that the single-row form did not exist)
**Phase/PR:** `1740f226 feat(map-view): collapse the floating map chrome into a single-row search bar` (PR #127)

**Role:** One always-visible pill hosting the free-text location search, the clear-✕, a hairline divider, and the filter-sheet entry point with its active-count badge.

**"Collapsed" vs "expanded" — the honest answer.** There is **no collapse/expand animation and no collapsed-icon state**. The search bar is a *single persistent row* whose contents change conditionally. What "collapsed" means in the PR title is **the whole chrome collapsing from three rows to one**, not the search field toggling between a magnifier icon and a field. Downstream: do NOT build a tap-to-expand search affordance in the demo — there isn't one.

The two conditional states within the row:

**State A — resting / empty search** (`searchText.length === 0`):
```
[← close]  [🔍  Search locations...            │  ⚙ ]
```
- `Ionicons "search"` 16pt at `textSecondary`, `marginRight: 6`
- `TextInput` flex-1, full pill height, `fontSize: 14`, colour `textPrimary`, placeholder `"Search locations..."` at `placeholderColor`
- **no** clear button
- `filterDivider` 1×22 at `borderColor`
- `Ionicons "options-outline"` 20pt at `textPrimary` in a 44pt-wide `inlineButton`

**State B — text entered** (`searchText.length > 0`), `MapControls.tsx:152-162`:
```
[← close]  [🔍  precinct            ✕  │  ⚙ ]
```
Adds a `Pressable testID="map-search-clear"` before the divider: `Ionicons "close-circle"` 18pt at `textSecondary`, in the same 44pt `inlineButton`. `onPress={() => onSearchChange('')}`.

**Badge state** (independent of A/B), `MapControls.tsx:178-185`:
```jsx
{filterBadgeCount > 0 && (
  <View
    testID="map-filter-badge"
    style={[styles.badge, { backgroundColor: primaryAccent }]}
  >
    <Text style={styles.badgeText}>{filterBadgeCount}</Text>
  </View>
)}
```
Absolutely positioned inside the filter `inlineButton` at `top: 6, right: 4`; 16×16 minimum, radius 9999, `paddingHorizontal: 4`; fill `#2B8CC1` dark / `#1e3a8a` light; label 10px `700` `#ffffff`.

**The close button is conditional**, `MapControls.tsx:114-129`: rendered only when `onClose` is supplied. 44×44 circle, same `surfaceBg` + `borderColor` + `surfaceShadow` as the pill, `Ionicons "arrow-back"` 20pt at `textPrimary`.

**The proximity chip row** (`MapControls.tsx:192-225`) is the second, conditional row — only while `proximityActive`:
```
[◎ 2 km · 5 of 9   ✕]
```
- Container: `styles.chip` + `surfaceShadow` + `{ backgroundColor: surfaceBg, borderColor }` — height 44, radius 9999, 1px border, self-sized (row is `flexDirection: 'row'` so the chip hugs its content and left-aligns).
- Body `Pressable testID="proximity-chip"` → `onOpenFilters` — `Ionicons "locate-outline"` 15pt at `primaryAccent`, then `Text` `{proximityRadius} km · {filteredCount} of {locationCount}` at `textPrimary`, 12px `600`, `gap: 6`, `paddingLeft: 12`.
- Dismiss `Pressable testID="proximity-chip-dismiss"` → `onProximityDeactivate` — `Ionicons "close-circle"` 18pt at `textSecondary`, 44pt min-width.

Both rows sit inside `innerPadding` with `gap: Layout.spacing.sm` = 8 between them, under `paddingTop: safeAreaTop` on the transparent absolutely-positioned `outerContainer` at `zIndex: 1020`, `pointerEvents="box-none"` throughout so map gestures pass through the gaps.

**What it replaced.** The baseline search field was a bare pill on **row 2**, height 36, radius 20, `paddingHorizontal: 12`, painted with the now-deleted `inputBg` token, with **no leading icon, no clear button, no divider, and no filter entry** — the filters were the eight-to-nine sibling pills across rows 1 and 3. There was no close/back button in the chrome at all; changing case went through `MapHost`'s separate absolutely-positioned pill.

### `MapFiltersSheet` — `src/features/location/map-view/components/MapFiltersSheet.tsx`

**Status:** **NEW since baseline** (291 lines, entirely new file)
**Phase/PR:** `41b27af3 feat(map-view): add MapFiltersSheet — status + proximity filters in a themed glass sheet` (PR #127), then `487924b6` (shared `ALL_LOCATION_STATUSES`), `6e10eea3`, `a9451287` (test-only).

**Role:** A `GlassBottomSheet` modal holding everything that used to float over the tiles as pills — the three status filters, the proximity on/off switch, the four radius presets, and a Clear All / Done footer.

#### What it filters

Three things, in this order down the sheet:

1. **Location Status** — a wrap row of three toggle chips built from `ALL_LOCATION_STATUSES` (`['started','working','complete']`, `constants/index.ts:387-391`). Multi-select; each tap emits the **full updated array** via `onStatusToggle`. Empty array = no status filter.
2. **Proximity** — a labelled row ("Filter by radius") with the shared `<Switch>`. Flipping it calls `onProximityToggle`; the host resolves GPS/centroid asynchronously.
3. **Radius presets** — a wrap row of four chips (`0.5 / 1 / 2 / 5 km` from `PROXIMITY_PRESETS`), **rendered only while `proximityActive`**. Single-select via `onRadiusChange`.

Plus a static hint line and a two-button footer.

**Search text is NOT here** — it stays in the map search bar (`MapControls`). That split is the whole point of the redesign.

#### How it opens

Host-owned boolean. `MapHost.tsx:163-167` declares `filtersVisible` + `handleOpenFilters` / `handleCloseFilters`; `MapControls`' filter button (`testID="map-open-filters"`) and the proximity chip body (`testID="proximity-chip"`) both call `onOpenFilters`. `MapHost.tsx:523-538`:

```jsx
<MapFiltersSheet
  visible={filtersVisible}
  onClose={handleCloseFilters}
  activeStatuses={filters.statuses ?? []}
  onStatusToggle={setStatusFilter}
  proximityActive={proximityIsActive}
  proximityRadius={proximityRadiusKm}
  onProximityToggle={() => void handleProximityToggle()}
  onRadiusChange={proximitySetRadius}
  onClearAll={handleClearAllFilters}
  locationCount={locationCount}
  filteredCount={filteredCount}
/>
```

Four ways to close, all routed to the same `onClose` (`MapFiltersSheet.tsx:47`): *"Backdrop tap, swipe-down, Android back, and the Done button."*

#### Canonical recipe NOW

**Shell configuration**, `MapFiltersSheet.tsx:101-130`:
```jsx
<GlassBottomSheet
  visible={visible}
  onClose={onClose}
  title="Map Filters"
  subtitle={subtitle}
  closeLabel="Close map filters"
  testID="map-filters-sheet"
  footer={ ... }
>
```

**Notes.** File-header docblock, `MapFiltersSheet.tsx:10-18`, is the design record for the colour choices:
> Theming: this is app chrome, not map chrome (same D3(a) reasoning as the locations bottom sheet) — it reads useTheme() directly and follows the app theme. Status toggles use the D8(a) severity token pairs (`{severity}Light` fill + `{severity}OnLight` foreground) via STATUS_SEVERITY, mirroring SheetHandle's badges and Banner, so the same LocationStatus reads identically here and in the sheet legend. The unselected dot uses STATUS_ACCENT — the bare-mark tokens that clear WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 floor on the sheet surface.

This component reads `useTheme()` **directly** (`:81`), unlike `MapControls`/`MapScaleBar` which take `isDark` as a prop.

### `MapBottomSheet` — `src/features/location/map-view/components/MapBottomSheet.tsx`

**Status:** CHANGED (54 lines touched)
**Phase/PR:** `6fb6f839 refactor(map-view): make the bottom sheet theme-aware (D3a)`, `ad62ecb2`, `145f7ea4 fix(map-sheet): patch gorhom to stop animating layout during the drag`, `7ab76a9b`, `069e0faa`, `d1739700`.

**Role:** The `@gorhom/bottom-sheet` container — three detents, stable handle identity, theme-aware surface, and the list↔detail switch.

**Canonical recipe NOW.**

`StyleSheet.create`, `MapBottomSheet.tsx:249-262`, VERBATIM:
```js
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  // The shadow comes from Layout.shadow.sheet (the token Phase 0 lifted out of
  // GlassBottomSheet) rather than this file's own #000/-6/0.35/r16/e20 recipe,
  // which was one of nine competing shadow recipes in the app.
  sheet: {
    borderTopLeftRadius: Layout.borderRadius.sheet,
    borderTopRightRadius: Layout.borderRadius.sheet,
    borderTopWidth: 1,
  },
  divider: {
    height: 1,
    marginHorizontal: Layout.spacing.lg,
  },
})
```

Applied style array, `MapBottomSheet.tsx:182-210`:
```jsx
style={[
  styles.sheet,
  Layout.shadow.sheet[colorScheme],
  {
    backgroundColor: SHEET_SURFACE_COLORS[colorScheme].backgroundGradient[0],
    borderTopColor: GlassColors[colorScheme].sheet.border,
  },
]}
```

Resolved:
- radius **22** top-left/top-right, `borderTopWidth: 1`
- `borderTopColor` = `rgba(100, 116, 139, 0.4)` light / `rgba(28, 78, 132, 0.6)` dark
- `backgroundColor` = `#ffffff` light / `#002853` dark (the gradient's own first stop)
- shadow light: `rgba(30, 58, 138, 0.15)`, offset `{0,-8}`, opacity 1, radius 28; dark: `#000`, offset `{0,-8}`, opacity 0.5, radius 40

The `backgroundColor` carries a load-bearing comment, `MapBottomSheet.tsx:186-206`, explaining why the surface must be **opaque**:
> NOT redundant, despite SheetBackground painting over it. This is the node @gorhom applies `style` to (BottomSheetBody), and it is the node that translates every drag frame -- so it is the node carrying `Layout.shadow.sheet` above. iOS only uses the cheap analytic `shadowPath` when the shadowed view's OWN background is opaque (RCTViewComponentView.mm, "Stage 1. Shadow Path": `CGColorGetAlpha(_backgroundColor.CGColor) > 0.999`). Without it RN sets `shadowPath = nil` and Core Animation falls back to a pixel-derived shadow: it renders this view's ENTIRE subtree offscreen to derive the shadow's alpha mask. gorhom re-lays-out that subtree every frame (BottomSheetContent animates `height` and `paddingBottom` off `animatedPosition`), so the offscreen buffer can never be cached and gets rebuilt at 60-120Hz over a live Mapbox GL surface. That is the drag jank.

**Divider**, `MapBottomSheet.tsx:213-216`:
```jsx
<View
  testID="sheet-divider"
  style={[styles.divider, { backgroundColor: withAlpha(colors.border, 0.5) }]}
/>
```
= `rgba(229, 231, 235, 0.5)` light / `rgba(28, 78, 132, 0.5)` dark, 1px tall, 24px horizontal margin.

**Sheet configuration**, `MapBottomSheet.tsx:83` and `:168-181`:
```js
const snapPoints = [SHEET_SNAP_POINTS.peek, SHEET_SNAP_POINTS.partial, SHEET_SNAP_POINTS.full]
// = [88, '40%', '65%']
```
```jsx
<BottomSheet
  ref={sheetRef}
  snapPoints={snapPoints}
  index={SHEET_INDEX.PEEK}          // 0
  enableDynamicSizing={false}
  onChange={onSheetChange}
  handleComponent={ConnectedSheetHandle}
  backgroundComponent={SheetBackground}
  style={...}
>
```
`enableDynamicSizing={false}` rationale, `:172-177`:
> @gorhom/bottom-sheet v5 defaults enableDynamicSizing to TRUE, which measures the content and injects an extra content-height detent into the snap array. That makes the SHEET_INDEX positions (PEEK/PARTIAL/FULL) drift with list length, so imperative snapToIndex calls landed on a count-dependent position. Disabling it pins the sheet to exactly the three configured snap points for deterministic positioning.

**Stable handle identity** — `ConnectedSheetHandle` is declared once at module scope (`:124-133`) and reads its live summary from `SheetSummaryContext` (`:100-104`). `:106-119` explains: a changing `handleComponent` *type* remounts the whole handle subtree including the `LinearGradient` accent strip — "the source of the peek-bar flicker on tap/back/filter."

Detail card is keyed, `:228` — `key={selectedLocation.id}` so switching locations resets the multi-scope expand state.

**What it replaced.** Baseline `StyleSheet.create` (`git show d9606460:...:213-230`):
```js
  sheet: {
    borderTopLeftRadius: 22,
    borderTopRightRadius: 22,
    shadowColor: '#000',
    shadowOffset: { width: 0, height: -6 },
    shadowOpacity: 0.35,
    shadowRadius: 16,
    elevation: 20,
    borderTopWidth: 1,
    borderTopColor: SHEET_SURFACE_COLORS.borderTop,      // 'rgba(30, 58, 95, 0.55)'
  },
  divider: {
    height: 1,
    backgroundColor: SHEET_SURFACE_COLORS.divider,       // 'rgba(30, 58, 95, 0.50)'
    marginHorizontal: Layout.spacing.lg,
  },
```
So: hardcoded 22 → `Layout.borderRadius.sheet`; a local `#000 / {0,-6} / 0.35 / r16 / e20` shadow → `Layout.shadow.sheet[colorScheme]` (offset −8, radius 28/40, per-theme colour); always-dark `borderTopColor` and `divider` → theme-derived. No `backgroundColor` on the sheet node at all at baseline (the jank fix added it).

**Notes.** `145f7ea4` ships `patches/@gorhom+bottom-sheet+5.2.14.patch` — native-only, nothing to port.

**Canonical recipe NOW.** The entire component body, `SheetBackground.tsx:26-44`, VERBATIM:
```jsx
export function SheetBackground({ style }: BottomSheetBackgroundProps): React.JSX.Element {
  const { colorScheme } = useTheme()

  return (
    <LinearGradient
      colors={[...SHEET_SURFACE_COLORS[colorScheme].backgroundGradient]}
      locations={[...SHEET_SURFACE_COLORS.backgroundGradientLocations]}
      start={{ x: 0, y: 0 }}
      end={{ x: 0, y: 1 }}
      style={[
        style,
        {
          borderTopLeftRadius: Layout.borderRadius.sheet,
          borderTopRightRadius: Layout.borderRadius.sheet,
        },
      ]}
    />
  )
}
```

Resolved gradients (stops at `[0, 0.5, 1]`, top→bottom):
- **light:** `#ffffff` → `#f9fafb` → `#ffffff`
- **dark:** `#002853` → `#0e3965` → `#002853`

Top corners **22**. Fully opaque in both themes.

**What it replaced.** Baseline was a single always-dark constant array `['rgb(13, 27, 42)', 'rgb(16, 30, 46)', 'rgb(10, 22, 36)']` with hardcoded `borderTopLeftRadius: 22 / borderTopRightRadius: 22` and no theme fork. The file docblock also dropped the *"matches the MediaLibrarySheet's deep navy fade aesthetic"* line.

The three-stop rationale, `constants/index.ts:345-348`:
> The three stops are background -> backgroundSecondary -> background: a subtle fade that returns to the base tone, replacing three hand-written navies (rgb(0,40,83) / rgb(4,46,91) / rgb(0,34,73)) that were an undeclared copy of the badge-blue ramp.

### `LocationRow` — `src/features/location/map-view/components/LocationRow.tsx`

**Status:** CHANGED — heavily (419 lines touched)
**Phase/PR:** `457b6427 fix(map-view): restore the glass fill on selected location rows` (PR #118, ruling D1a), `a9f28db4`, `694ce013 fix(theme): give status dots an accent that survives on a theme-aware surface`, `ad62ecb2`, `737a7336`, `069e0faa`, `efb2cbc3`, then **`7df5148b style(map): draw card borders on all four sides, drop the left accent bar`** (PR #127), `d1739700`.

**Role:** One memoized glass-card row in the sheet's location list. Two variants behind one export: location and incident.

#### THE RULING-VS-CODE SEQUENCE — flagged explicitly

The brief is right that there is a conflict, and it goes **further than the brief describes**. Three states, in order:

1. **Baseline (`d9606460`).** Selection **replaced the fill**: the glass gradient was swapped for a status-tinted one. `git show d9606460:.../LocationRow.tsx:56-60`:
   ```js
   const gradientColors: [string, string] = isSelected
     ? [
         SHEET_SURFACE_COLORS.rowSelectedGlassStart(statusColor),   // `${color}10`  = 6% alpha
         SHEET_SURFACE_COLORS.rowSelectedGlassEnd(statusColor),     // `${color}18`  = 9% alpha
       ]
     : [ ... ]
   ```

2. **Ruling D1(a), landed by `457b6427` (PR #118).** "Keep the glass fill; tint the border + 4px left accent." Implemented exactly: uniform glass gradient in both states, `borderColor: isSelected ? statusColor : glass.border`, and a reserved 4px left edge painted `transparent` when unselected. The docblock written for that state is the one still at the **top of the current file**.

3. **PR #127, `7df5148b`.** The 4px left accent is **DROPPED**, and — this is the part beyond the brief — **selection is no longer indicated on the row at all.**

**ANSWER: the left accent bar does NOT survive on `LocationRow`.** Nor does any other selected-row treatment. Current code, `LocationRow.tsx:86-92`, VERBATIM — no `isSelected` anywhere in the style:
```jsx
<LinearGradient
  testID="location-row-card"
  colors={[...glass.gradient]}
  start={{ x: 0, y: 0 }}
  end={{ x: 0, y: 1 }}
  style={[styles.card, { borderColor: glass.border }]}
>
  {children}
</LinearGradient>
```
`isSelected` now feeds **only** `accessibilityState={{ selected: isSelected }}` (`LocationRow.tsx:79`). A selected row is visually identical to an unselected one.

The design record for that, `LocationRow.tsx:51-57`:
> The border is UNIFORM. It used to reserve a 4px left edge and tint it with the status colour when selected, which left the unselected rows reading as though their left border were missing - the reserved edge was painted `transparent`. **Selection is not indicated here at all now: tapping a row opens that location's own sheet, which is the signal.**

**DOCBLOCK CONFLICT — a real, live staleness in the phone repo.** `LocationRow.tsx:11-18` (the file-header docblock) was **not updated** by `7df5148b` and still describes the superseded D1(a) state:
```
 * Selection (ruling D1a) ADDS to the row rather than replacing it: the glass
 * fill is untouched, the border takes the location's full-saturation status
 * colour and a 4px left accent lights up. The 4px left border is reserved at
 * all times (`borderLeftColor: 'transparent'` when unselected, which reveals
 * the gradient behind it) so selecting a row cannot reflow its content. The
 * previous treatment swapped the opaque gradient for a 6%/9%-alpha status tint,
 * which made the fill vanish and left selection reading as an outline-only
 * downgrade.
```
The `GlassRowShell` docblock 34 lines below it (`:45-57`) contradicts it, and **`GlassRowShell` is what the code does**. Whoever ports this must read the shell's docblock, not the file header.

#### Canonical recipe NOW

`GlassRowShell`, `LocationRow.tsx:58-98`, VERBATIM:
```jsx
function GlassRowShell({
  isSelected,
  onPress,
  accessibilityLabel,
  children,
}: {
  isSelected: boolean
  onPress: () => void
  accessibilityLabel: string
  children: React.ReactNode
}): React.JSX.Element {
  const { colors, colorScheme } = useTheme()
  const glass = GlassColors[colorScheme].card

  return (
    <Pressable
      testID="location-row"
      onPress={onPress}
      style={({ pressed }) => [styles.pressable, pressed && styles.rowPressed]}
      android_ripple={{ color: withAlpha(colors.text, 0.08) }}
      accessibilityRole="button"
      accessibilityState={{ selected: isSelected }}
      accessibilityLabel={accessibilityLabel}
    >
      <View style={[styles.shadowWrapper, Layout.shadow.card[colorScheme]]}>
        {/* Top highlight edge */}
        <View style={[styles.highlight, { backgroundColor: glass.highlightTop }]} />

        <LinearGradient
          testID="location-row-card"
          colors={[...glass.gradient]}
          start={{ x: 0, y: 0 }}
          end={{ x: 0, y: 1 }}
          style={[styles.card, { borderColor: glass.border }]}
        >
          {children}
        </LinearGradient>
      </View>
    </Pressable>
  )
}
```

Resolved surface, per theme (`GlassColors[scheme].card`):

| | light | dark |
|---|---|---|
| gradient (vertical) | `rgba(248, 250, 252, 1)` → `rgba(241, 245, 249, 1)` | `rgba(14, 57, 101, 0.85)` → `rgba(23, 65, 110, 0.92)` |
| border (all four sides, 1px) | `rgba(148, 163, 184, 0.45)` | `rgba(28, 78, 132, 0.5)` |
| `highlightTop` (1px strip) | `rgba(148, 163, 184, 0.45)` | `rgba(184, 212, 240, 0.08)` |
| shadow | `rgba(30, 58, 138, 0.18)`, `{0,3}`, op 1, r 8, elev 4 | `#000`, `{0,4}`, op 0.15, r 8, elev 4 |
| android ripple | `rgba(17, 24, 39, 0.08)` | `rgba(240, 244, 248, 0.08)` |

```js
// `STATUS_ACCENT`, not `PIN_COLORS`. This dot and D1(a)'s selection border

// `working` 2.87:1 DARK against WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1. (DEF-UI-017.)
const accentToken = STATUS_ACCENT[location.status]
```

**What it replaced.** Baseline (`git show d9606460:.../LocationDetailCard.tsx:769-…`) — every colour was `Colors.dark.*` or `SHEET_SURFACE_COLORS.*`, so the card rendered identically in light mode:

Now `<Button variant="ghost" size="small">` with the chevron inside the label string (`:250-254`: *"that pill was one of six local button implementations on this screen, and the shared control brings the 44pt touch target and haptics with it"*).
- `locationName` **`fontSize: 22`** (now 24), `color: Colors.dark.text`
- `statusBadge` `paddingVertical: 4, paddingHorizontal: 10, borderRadius: 10, gap: 6` and **no border** (now `paddingHorizontal: 8` + `borderWidth: 1`); colours from `PIN_COLORS`
- `statusDot` `borderRadius: 3` (now `full`); `statusBadgeText` **`fontSize: 11`** (now 12)
- `addressCard` was a **flat wash**: `backgroundColor: SHEET_SURFACE_COLORS.infoBg` = `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.04)`, `borderRadius: 12, padding: 14, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: SHEET_SURFACE_COLORS.divider` = `rgba(30, 58, 95, 0.50)`. Now `<Card glass glassVariant="nestedCard">`. Same for the scope / requester / contact cards, which were at radii **12/10/10/10** (see the styles docblock).
- `addressEmoji` `fontSize: 16, marginRight: 10` (now 8); `addressText` `lineHeight: 20` (now 21); `cityText` `fontSize: 12`
- `incidentTypeChip` **`fontSize: 11`**, `color: PIN_COLORS.incident`, `backgroundColor: \`${PIN_COLORS.incident}25\`` (15% alpha). Now 12px with the `errorLight`/`errorOnLight` pair.
- the CTAs were **locally-authored `LinearGradient` buttons**: `colors={[...CTA_GRADIENT_COLORS]}` = `['#1a8fc2', '#1580b0', '#0f6f9e']`, `start={{x:0,y:0}} end={{x:1,y:1}}`, with `ctaShadow` = `rgba(0, 191, 255, 0.25)`. Both constants are now **deleted**.

**Notes.** `7aa75581` records a real RN trap worth carrying into the demo, `:967-974`:
> The 8pt between the icon and the label rides on the icon, not on a `gap` in `camerasToggleCard`. `<Card>` routes only flexDirection / alignItems / justifyContent / flexWrap and the padding family into its gradient; `gap` lands on the outer wrapper, whose one in-flow child is that gradient, where it does nothing. It read as working and rendered 0pt. See `cardStack` above for the same trap, and **DEF-UI-013** for the routing gap itself.

`:955-958` — the cameras toggle's `hitSlop` was **removed**, not forgotten: *"minHeight clears the 44pt touch target on its own now that the hitSlop is gone: the Card fills the Pressable, so slop reaching outside it was never dispatched on Android."* Same reasoning as `MapControls.inlineButton`.

`:987-989` — `cardLabel` uses `textSecondary` not `textTertiary`: *"the tertiary token is a documented sub-AA ceiling (M2b) and these labels are read, not skimmed."*

`StyleSheet.create`, `CameraMarker.tsx:120-192`, VERBATIM:

```js
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: {
    alignItems: 'center',

  glyphBase: {

    maxWidth: 360,
    paddingVertical: Layout.spacing.sm,
    paddingHorizontal: Layout.spacing.base,
    borderRadius: Layout.borderRadius.md,
    borderWidth: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth,
    backgroundColor: CAMERA_MARKER.calloutBg,
    borderColor: CAMERA_MARKER.calloutBorder,
  },

    fontWeight: Typography.fontWeight.semibold,
    textAlign: 'center',
  },
  calloutMeta: {
    color: CAMERA_MARKER.calloutTextDim,
    fontSize: 11,
    textAlign: 'center',
    marginTop: 1,
  },
  /** Lat/lon line — monospace so the digits align, and full-brightness text
   *  because the coordinate is primary forensic data (not dimmed meta). */
  calloutCoords: {
    color: CAMERA_MARKER.calloutText,
    fontSize: 11,
    fontFamily: Typography.fontFamily.mono,
    textAlign: 'center',
    marginTop: Layout.spacing.xxs,
  },

```

Resolved: base **30×30**, radius 15, fill `#ffffff`, border **1.5px `rgba(0, 40, 83, 0.55)`**, `#000` shadow `{0,1}` op 0.3 r 2, elev 3. Glyph = `MaterialCommunityIcons "cctv"` at **18px**, colour `#111111`. Callout sits at `bottom: 34`, `minWidth: 120`, `maxWidth: 360`, padding **8/12**, radius **8**, hairline border; fill `rgba(0, 40, 83, 0.95)` (= `MAP_SURFACE_COLORS.controlsBg`), border `rgba(28, 78, 132, 0.6)` (= `.borderStrong`). Callout name **13px `600` `#ffffff`**; meta **11px `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.7)`**; coords **11px monospace `#ffffff`**. `hitSlop={8}`.

Callout content order: name (falls back to `'Camera'` on empty/whitespace) → resolution? → `lat, lng` (6dp) → `±{accuracy}m` (1dp).

**What it replaced.** Only the `baseBorder` value moved, and only because `Colors.dark.background` moved: `rgba(13, 27, 42, 0.55)` → `rgba(0, 40, 83, 0.55)` (the badge-blue recolor, `68f4e18a`). Likewise `calloutBg` `rgba(13, 27, 42, 0.95)` → `rgba(0, 40, 83, 0.95)` and `calloutBorder` `rgba(30, 58, 95, 0.6)` → `rgba(28, 78, 132, 0.6)`. Everything else is a literal-to-token substitution at identical values: `paddingVertical: 8`→`spacing.sm`, `paddingHorizontal: 12`→`spacing.base`, `borderRadius: 8`→`borderRadius.md`, `fontWeight: '600'`→`Typography.fontWeight.semibold`, `fontFamily: 'monospace'`→`Typography.fontFamily.mono`, `marginTop: 2`→`spacing.xxs`. The barrel icon import became a subpath import.

**Notes.** The `overflow: 'visible'` comment (`:124-128`) is a genuine cross-platform trap; irrelevant for a web demo but worth knowing the callout is deliberately drawn outside its parent's bounds. `fontSize: 13` and `fontSize: 11` here are two of the 19 off-scale sizes named in campaign row **DEF-UI-027** (no `Typography.fontSize` step lands on 10/11/13/15/22).

```js
/** Teardrop ratio of the source viewBox (24 wide × 36 tall). */
const PIN_VIEWBOX_WIDTH = 24
const PIN_VIEWBOX_HEIGHT = 36
```

```jsx
  {/* Teardrop body — incident colour with a white stroke so it reads on
      both light streets and dark satellite tiles. */}
  <Path d={TEARDROP_PATH} fill={color} stroke="#ffffff" strokeWidth={1.5} />
```

Resolved: default height **46**, width `46 × (24/36)` ≈ **30.67**. **Role:** The `SymbolLayer` that draws the cluster count over the cluster circle.

**Canonical recipe NOW.** `ClusterBadge.tsx:222-247`, VERBATIM:
```jsx
export function ClusterBadge({ sourceID }: ClusterBadgeProps): React.JSX.Element {
  return (
    <Mapbox.SymbolLayer
      id="cluster-count"
      sourceID={sourceID}
      filter={['has', 'point_count']}
      style={{
        textField: ['get', 'point_count_abbreviated'],
        textFont: ['DIN Offc Pro Medium', 'Arial Unicode MS Bold'],
        textSize: ['step', ['get', 'point_count'], 12, 10, 14, 50, 16],
        textColor: '#FFFFFF',
        textHaloColor: 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)',
        textHaloWidth: 1,
        textIgnorePlacement: true,
        textAllowOverlap: true,
      }}
    />
  )
}
```
*(file-local lines 30-55.)*

Text scales **12 → 14 at ≥10 points → 16 at ≥50 points**, matching the circle's `16 → 22 → 28` radius steps. Always `#FFFFFF` with a `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)` 1px halo — theme-invariant.

**What it replaced.** Identical values; only the `textSize` array was reflowed onto one line.

**Notes.** Two load-bearing comments to carry over. `:231-237`:
> Explicit Mapbox-SERVED font stack. Without it, the SDK's default font produces no glyphs under satellite-streets-v12 and the count text silently never renders (the circle still draws — it needs no glyphs)… Do NOT use a locally-installed device font here — that triggers rnmapbox/maps#309, which hides the text instead.

And `:200-207` on `sourceID` forwarding: `ShapeSource` injects `sourceID` onto its **direct children only** (`cloneReactChildrenWithProps`, no recursion), so this wrapper must pass it through or the layer never binds and silently labels nothing.

### `MapScaleBar` — `src/features/location/map-view/components/MapScaleBar.tsx`

**Status:** CHANGED (25 lines touched)
**Phase/PR:** `a1f6c195 fix(map-view): keep the scale bar on white in dark mode and document the D3a split` (PR #118), `eb261c52`, `d1739700`.

**Role:** A fixed-width custom scale bar in the map's bottom-left, replacing the native Mapbox ornament.

**Canonical recipe NOW.** Theme-aware via the `isDark` **prop** (same pattern as `MapControls`, not a context read).

Colour derivation, `MapScaleBar.tsx:140-151`, VERBATIM:
```js
const pillBg = isDark ? MAP_GLASS_COLORS.containerBgDark : MAP_GLASS_COLORS.containerBgLight
const borderColor = isDark ? MAP_GLASS_COLORS.borderDark : MAP_GLASS_COLORS.borderLight
// Text and rule colour. The light value used to be an inline Tailwind
// slate-900 (rgba(15,23,42,·)), a colour that appears nowhere in Colors.light;
// it is now Colors.light.text, the same token MapControls uses for its pill
// labels. Dark stays on `onPrimary` (white) rather than moving to
// Colors.dark.text: over a bright satellite tile the softer text token
// measures 3.70:1 against this pill versus white's 4.05:1, and this surface
// has no contrast headroom to give away. Alphas are unchanged in both.
const baseText = isDark ? Colors.dark.onPrimary : Colors.light.text
const textColor = withAlpha(baseText, isDark ? 0.85 : 0.8)
const lineColor = withAlpha(baseText, isDark ? 0.7 : 0.65)
```

Resolved:

| | dark | light |
|---|---|---|
| `pillBg` | `rgba(0, 40, 83, 0.82)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.92)` |
| `borderColor` | `rgba(28, 78, 132, 0.45)` | `rgba(100, 116, 139, 0.35)` |
| `textColor` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.85)` | `rgba(17, 24, 39, 0.8)` |
| `lineColor` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.7)` | `rgba(17, 24, 39, 0.65)` |

**The updated peek-height arithmetic**, `:300-311`, VERBATIM — it changed with the handle geometry:
```
   * Fixed peek height — two-line layout (recomputed after the handle geometry
   * was matched to GlassBottomSheet and the type scale was tokenised):
   *   accent strip:  2pt
   *   pill row:      8pt paddingTop + 4pt pill + 4pt paddingBottom = 16pt
   *   title line:    ~24pt (fontSize.lg = 18, bold)
   *   title→badge gap: 4pt (Layout.spacing.xs)
   *   badge line:    ~22pt (2pt padV * 2 + 1pt border * 2 + ~16pt text)
   *   bottom pad:    8pt (Layout.spacing.sm)
   *   ────────────
   *   Total:         ~76pt  →  held at 88pt for rendering variance
```
Baseline read: `accent strip: 1pt / pill row: 14+4+10 = 28pt / title ~22pt (fontSize 17) / gap 4pt / badge ~18pt / bottom 8pt / Total ~81pt → rounded to 88pt`. **The 88pt value is unchanged in both** — only the derivation moved.

**What it replaced — the baseline diff, exhaustively.**

**Notes.** `PIN_COLORS`' docblock, `:46-57`, is the D8 record:
> Status pin palette (D8). Derived from the dark status tokens rather than the iOS system palette it used to hardcode (#FF9500 / #00BFFF / #34C759 / #e53935). These colours drive more than the map pins — the LocationRow status dot, the LocationDetailCard status badge, the SheetHandle count badges and the MapControls filter pills all read from here — so an independent palette meant the same `LocationStatus` rendered in one colour on the map and another in `CaseStatusBadge`. `Colors.dark` (not the active scheme) because the pins are painted onto satellite tiles, which never follow the app theme.

**That docblock is now partly stale**: the LocationRow dot, the detail-card badge, the SheetHandle badges and the (deleted) MapControls filter pills **no longer read `PIN_COLORS`** — they read `STATUS_ACCENT` / `STATUS_SEVERITY` (see `status-severity.ts`). `PIN_COLORS`' live consumers today are the GL `STATUS_COLOR_EXPRESSION`, `IncidentMarker`'s default `color`, and `LocationRow`'s `fallback` branch.

`CLUSTER_CIRCLE_STYLE`'s colour rationale, `:215-221`:
> Dark translucent, borderless — matches the app's dark-glass chrome (the floating MapControls + callout bubbles use this same navy via MAP_SURFACE_COLORS), so clusters read as neutral map chrome rather than a fourth status colour competing with the blue "working" pins. Opacity is the dial: translucent enough to sense the map through it, opaque enough to hold on dark satellite imagery (no border to lean on). The white, halo'd count label (ClusterBadge) reads cleanly on top — left untouched.

`SHEET_SURFACE_COLORS`' D3(a) + opacity record, `:326-348`:
> Ruling D3(a): the sheet is app chrome, not map chrome. It covers up to 65% of the screen, so it follows the app theme even though the satellite tiles behind it cannot. Everything the sheet used to source from an always-dark constant (accent strip, top border, handle, divider) is now derived from `useTheme()` at the call site; only the gradient survives as a constant, because of the opacity requirement below.
>
> Fully opaque (alpha 1.0) on purpose, in BOTH themes: … At 0.97-0.99 the translucency was visually imperceptible but not free; opaque lets the compositor occlude the map region behind the sheet. This is why the sheet does NOT use `GlassColors[scheme].sheet`, whose dark gradient starts at 0.98 alpha.

`ALL_LOCATION_STATUSES`' rationale, `:372-391`:
> Pinned with `satisfies` so adding a fourth status is a COMPILE error here rather than a silent gap. `LocationStatus[]` alone accepts any subset, so the two hand-maintained copies this replaces (`MapFiltersSheet`'s `ALL_STATUSES` and `SheetHandle`'s `STATUS_KEYS`) would each have compiled clean while leaving the new status unfilterable in the sheet and absent from the legend - and `MapFiltersSheet`'s "N of M shown" subtitle would have reported a count the user could not reconcile.

### `utils/status-severity.ts` — `src/features/location/map-view/utils/status-severity.ts`

**Status:** **NEW since baseline** (72 lines, entirely new file)
**Phase/PR:** `a9f28db4 fix(map-view): paint sheet status badges from the theme status pair, not PIN_COLORS` and `694ce013 fix(theme): give status dots an accent that survives on a theme-aware surface` (PR #118).

**Role:** The two lookup tables that let sheet-side UI paint a `LocationStatus` from theme tokens instead of the theme-invariant `PIN_COLORS`. **This is the single most important new file for demo colour parity** — every status colour inside the sheet and the filters modal routes through it.

**Canonical recipe NOW — the whole file's exports, VERBATIM** (`:27-72`):
```ts
export const STATUS_SEVERITY = {
  started: 'warning',
  working: 'info',
  complete: 'success',
  /** Case-level incident rows and chips. */
  incident: 'error',
} as const satisfies Record<LocationStatus | 'incident', string>

export type StatusSeverity = (typeof STATUS_SEVERITY)[keyof typeof STATUS_SEVERITY]

export const STATUS_ACCENT = {
  started: 'warningAccent',
  working: 'infoDark',
  complete: 'successDark',
  /** Case-level incident rows and chips. */
  incident: 'error',
} as const satisfies Record<LocationStatus | 'incident', keyof ThemeColors>
```

**Usage contract, restated for the port:**
- A **badge / chip** (has a fill and text) uses `STATUS_SEVERITY[status]` → `colors[\`${sev}Light\`]` fill + `colors[sev]` border + `colors[\`${sev}OnLight\`]` foreground (dot AND label).
- A **bare dot** (no fill, no text) uses `STATUS_ACCENT[status]` → `colors[token]` directly.

Resolved `STATUS_ACCENT`:

| status | token | light | dark |
|---|---|---|---|
| `started` | `warningAccent` | `#b45309` | `#ffc62b` |
| `working` | `infoDark` | `#2563eb` | `#7a9fc4` |
| `complete` | `successDark` | `#059669` | `#0faa5e` |
| `incident` | `error` | `#ef4444` | `#ff4757` |

Resolved `STATUS_SEVERITY` pairs are the table in the `MapFiltersSheet` section.

**Consumers:** `MapFiltersSheet.tsx:41` (both), `LocationRow.tsx:37` (both), `SheetHandle.tsx` (`STATUS_SEVERITY`), `LocationDetailCard.tsx:35` (`STATUS_SEVERITY`).

**What it replaced.** Every one of those sites read `PIN_COLORS[status]` at baseline, with hand-written alpha suffixes (`${color}18`, `${color}35`, `${color}22`, `${color}25`, `${color}10`, `${color}12`, `${color}30`).

**Notes.** The whole file is a design record. `:5-11`:
> Why this exists: `PIN_COLORS` is deliberately theme-invariant (ruling D8a) — it paints elements rendered ONTO the satellite tiles, which never follow the app theme. Badge and chip text inside the bottom sheet is not on a tile, and once the sheet became theme-aware (D3a) those foregrounds collapsed in light mode: **`#ffd93d` on a 10%-alpha fill over white measures 1.33:1.** The `*Light` fill + `*OnLight` foreground pair Phase 0 added for exactly this measures **6.78-8.15:1 in light and 5.40-5.94:1 in dark.**

`:13-18`:
> Consumers mirror `Banner.tsx`, which is the same recipe at notice scale: `colors[{severity}Light]` fill, `colors[severity]` border (decorative - the fill and the label each carry the status independently), and `colors[{severity}OnLight]` for the text AND the dot. Banner documents why the saturated accent must not carry the foreground: it drops to **1.92-2.24:1** on its own tone in three of the four severities.

`:20-21`:
> `working` maps to `info` rather than `primary` because `primary` has no `*Light`/`*OnLight` pair — D8(a) only created them for the four severities.

`:37-64` on `STATUS_ACCENT`:
> A dot has no fill and no text: it is a bare mark on the sheet's own glass, so WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 non-text floor applies to the mark itself, and the `*Light` tones a badge uses are far too pale to carry it. … Reading `PIN_COLORS` for a dot inside the theme-aware sheet is what **measured `started` at 1.26:1 in light, `complete` at 1.84:1 in light and `working` at 2.87:1 in DARK.** … Measured on the worst stop of `card` and `sheet` in both themes, and pinned by `src/constants/__tests__/palette-contrast.test.ts`:
> ```
>   started   warningAccent   6.82 dark / 4.58 light
>   working   infoDark        3.87 dark / 4.72 light
>   complete  successDark     3.54 dark / 3.44 light
>   incident  error           3.21 dark / 3.44 light
> ```
> Four distinct hues, which is half the acceptance bar: a palette that clears 3:1 by collapsing to one colour passes the number and fails the user. (DEF-UI-017.)

**Role / behaviour to port:**

- `formatCoordinates(lat, lng, source?)` → `{ oneLine, sourceChip, ... }` at **6 decimal places**, finite-guarded. 87 lines. `oneLine` is what the coordinates row and the camera callout render.
- `getStatusLabel(status)` → `'Started' | 'Working' | 'Complete'` via an exhaustive switch with a `_exhaustive: never` guard. 33 lines.
- `copyCoordinatesToClipboard(lat, lng)` → clipboard + toast for `"lat, lng"`; refuses non-finite. 85 lines.

**Notes.** `formatCoordinates` takes **latitude first** while every GeoJSON coordinate in this sub-feature is `[longitude, latitude]` — every call site swaps explicitly (`coordinate[1], coordinate[0]`). README pitfall 6 (`:417`) names this as a live trap.

### Hooks — `useMapData` / `useMapFilter` / `useProximity` / `useBottomSheet` / `useCameraVisibility`

**Status:** UNCHANGED behaviourally. `useMapData.ts` (23 lines), `useMapFilter.ts` (11), `useProximity.ts` (9) are **prettier reflow only**, plus one comment and one `void`-adapter note in `useMapData`. `useBottomSheet.ts` and `useCameraVisibility.ts` do not appear in the delta at all.
**Phase/PR:** `d1739700`, `4794b024 fix(location): contain promise-family findings in map-view`.

**Role + contracts (from the README, unchanged):**
- `useMapData(caseId?, filters?)` → `{ collection, filteredCollection, isLoading, error, refresh, cameraBounds, initialCenter }`. Fetches on mount and on `caseId` change; **filters are a reactive parameter**, never owned here. Camera-fit values derive from a camera-stripped view so toggling cameras never re-fits.
- `useMapFilter()` → `{ filters, setStatusFilter, setSearchText, clearFilters, activeFilterCount }`. Single owner of `MapFilter`. Empty arrays / empty strings normalise to `undefined` and are not counted. **`activeFilterCount` is not consumed by `MapHost` any more** — the badge uses its own derivation.
- `useProximity(collection)` → `{ isActive, center, radiusKm, result, activate, deactivate, setRadius, setCenter }`. `deactivate()` preserves `center` + `radius` for re-activation. `result.locationCount` counts only `featureType === 'location'`.
- `useBottomSheet()` → `{ sheetRef, contentMode, selectedLocationId, selectLocation, showList, handleSheetChange, resetForNewCase, currentIndex }`. `selectLocation` / `showList` snap to PARTIAL; `handleSheetChange` resets to list mode **only** when the sheet collapses to PEEK while in detail mode.
- `useCameraVisibility()` → `{ isShown, toggle, reset }`. Host-owned, session-scoped, default off; **not barrel-exported**.

**Notes.** The only substantive change is a comment in `useMapData.ts` explaining why the mount effect's discarded promise is safe: *"`fetchData` cannot reject — its catch both logErrors and sets the `error` state the map renders — so the discarded promise carries no observable outcome."* Nothing here affects visual parity.

### `MapPicker` — `src/features/case-management/components/MapPicker.tsx`

**Status:** CHANGED — substantially (239 lines touched)
**Phase/PR:** `d6c8fe4f fix(case-management): give MapPicker rows a glass fill and a stable selection accent` (PR #118 owner addendum), `dd559beb`, `5eea966b fix(case-management): stop the focus refresh raising a pull-to-refresh spinner`, `130ce076 refactor(map-picker): name the header-spacer prop like its sibling (F16)`, `3af1f84e`, `04f07956 feat(map): give the Map tab the shared floating header`, **`7df5148b`** (the border rule), `d1739700`.

**Role:** The Map tab's content when no case is picked — an in-screen case list, not a modal.

#### THE ACCENT-BAR VERDICT HERE IS DIFFERENT FROM `LocationRow`

**MapPicker KEEPS a selection treatment; it just isn't a left bar any more.** `MapPicker.tsx:140-153`, VERBATIM:
```jsx
style={[
  styles.rowCard,
  {
    // Uniform on all four edges. This used to reserve a 4px LEFT
    // edge and paint it `transparent` when unselected, so every
    // unselected card read as though its left border were missing,
    // and the selected one wore a heavy bar down one side.
    // Selection is now the border's weight and colour, evenly:
    // 2px primary against 1px glass. The 1px difference reflows
    // the row's content by 1px on selection, which is the cost of
    // dropping the reserved edge and is not perceptible.
    borderWidth: isSelected ? 2 : 1,
    borderColor: isSelected ? colors.primary : rowGlass.border,
  },
]}
```
Plus the title recolours: `MapPicker.tsx:163` — `color: isSelected ? colors.primary : colors.text`.

So: **two surfaces, one commit, two outcomes.** `LocationRow` → selection invisible. `MapPicker` → 2px primary border on all four sides + primary title. Downstream must not unify these.

#### Canonical recipe NOW

Row surface, `MapPicker.tsx:100-103` and `:133-155`:
```js
const { colors, colorScheme } = useTheme()
// Rows are the nested tier (D13): a nestedCard gradient at radius `md`,
// inside the screen rather than inside another card.
const rowGlass = GlassColors[colorScheme ?? 'light'].nestedCard
```

```jsx
  <View style={[styles.rowHighlight, { backgroundColor: rowGlass.highlightTop }]} />
  <LinearGradient

    colors={rowGlass.gradient as [string, string]}
    start={{ x: 0, y: 0 }}
    end={{ x: 0, y: 1 }}
    style={[ styles.rowCard, { borderWidth: …, borderColor: … } ]}
  >
```

| border (unselected, 1px) | `rgba(100, 116, 139, 0.45)` | `rgba(43, 140, 193, 0.45)` |

Resolved: row `marginBottom: 8`; card radius **8** (`md`, the D13 nested-row tier), padding **16 vertical / 24 horizontal**, `minHeight: 56` (`touchTarget.large`); `rowTitle` **16px `600`**; `rowSubtitle` **14px**, `marginTop: 2`; `rowMeta` **12px**, `marginTop: 4`; list padding **24** all round; `statusContainer` 32/24 padding; `emptyTitle` 18px `600`; `emptySubtitle` 14px centred.

**Four render states**, `:192-273`: `!hasLoaded` → spinner + "Loading cases..."; `cases.length === 0 && error` → "Couldn't load cases" + error + Retry `<Button variant="primary">`; `cases.length === 0` → "No cases yet" / "Create a case from the Cases tab to get started."; else the list, optionally preceded by a stale-data `<Banner severity="error" message="Couldn't refresh. Showing the last loaded list.">` beside a `<Button variant="secondary" size="small">Retry</Button>`.

**What it replaced.**
- The row was `styles.row` **directly on the `Pressable`** with **no `backgroundColor` at all** — fully transparent against the screen's grid backdrop, held only by a 1px border. `:285-291` records the owner's verdict:
  > `styles.row` used to BE the whole row: no backgroundColor at all, so every row rendered fully transparent against the screen's grid backdrop with only a 1px border to hold it — **the surface the owner rated "really bad" (rulings addendum 1)**. It is now a glass card in the nested tier: a `GlassColors[scheme].nestedCard` gradient with the top highlight strip and card shadow, at radius `md` per D13.
- Selection was `borderLeftWidth: isSelected ? 4 : 1` with `borderColor: isSelected ? colors.primary : glassStyle.border` (`git show d9606460:...:122-127`).
- `rowMeta` read `colors.textTertiary`; now `colors.textSecondary`.
- There was a **local header inside the picker**: a `LinearGradient` block with `padding: 24`, `borderBottomWidth: 1`, title "Pick a Case" (`fontSize['2xl']`, bold) and subtitle "Select which case you'd like to view on the map." Deleted — `:190-191`: *"No local header. The tab route owns it now — the shared `MainHeader` inside `OverlayHeader`, same as every other tab."*
- Added props: `onScroll`, `ListHeaderComponent` (renamed from a differently-named spacer prop by `130ce076`).
- The error/empty branches and the stale-data `Banner` are new (`dd559beb`, BUG-033/BUG-037).

**Notes.** `:296-297` — why not `<Card glass glassVariant="nestedCard">`:
> Card pins its gradient to radius `lg` and owns `borderColor`, so it can express neither the nested tier's `md` nor the selection accent. Card itself belongs to Phase 9.

That is the same reason `LocationRow` hand-rolls `GlassRowShell`, at a different radius (`lg` = 12 there, `md` = 8 here) — the D13 depth tier (`Layout.ts:25-29`): *"md (8) nested ROWS … lg (12) cards, modals, form sections."*

### The unified card recipe — who consumes what

`Card.tsx` is a sibling agent's file, but the contract my files depend on, read at `src/components/common/Card.tsx` @ main:

- default props: `padding = 'md'` (line 47) → `Layout.spacing.md` = **16**; `glassVariant = 'card'` (line 51).
- `const shadowStyle: ViewStyle = Layout.shadow.card[isLightMode ? 'light' : 'dark']` (line 68).
- `styles.glassContainer` (223-227): `position:'relative'`, `borderRadius: Layout.borderRadius.lg` (**12**), `overflow:'hidden'`.
- `styles.highlight` (229-236): `position:'absolute'`, `top:0`, `left:0`, `right:0`, `height:1`, `zIndex:1`.
- `styles.gradient` (249-252): `borderRadius: Layout.borderRadius.lg` (**12**), `borderWidth: 1`.
- **The glass radius is `lg` (12) for EVERY variant, deliberately** — Card.tsx:239-248 documents that `glassVariant` carries depth in the GRADIENT, not the corner; keying the radius off the variant is explicitly forbidden without an owner decision (PR #114 finding F4). Mirrored in `Layout.ts:31-41`.

**Scoreboard for my scope:**

| File | Surface |
|---|---|
| `CaseCard.tsx:68` | `<Card style={styles.container} glass>` — default `card` variant |
| `DashboardCaseCard.tsx:160` | `<Card glass>` — default `card` variant |
| `CaseActionsSheet.tsx:289` | `<Card glass glassVariant="nestedCard" style={styles.reportCard}>` |
| `DeleteConfirmationModal.tsx:69` | `<Card style={styles.modal} glass glassVariant="elevated">` |
| `DeleteConfirmationModal.tsx:193-198` | `<Card glass glassVariant="nestedCard" style={styles.locationListCard} testID="location-list-card">` |
| `LocationItem.tsx` | **hand-rolled** — `View(surface) + View(highlight) + LinearGradient`, radius `md` (8) |
| `CompactLocationItem.tsx` | **hand-rolled** — same shape, radius `md` (8) |
| `LocationPill.tsx` | **hand-rolled** — `LinearGradient` only, radius `full` (9999) |
| `DashboardCaseCard.tsx` personnel chips | **hand-rolled** `LinearGradient`, radius `md` (8) |
| `CoordinateDisplay.tsx` | **hand-rolled** — `Pressable(container) + View(highlight) + LinearGradient`, radius `lg` (12) |
| `GpsCaptureControl.tsx` | **hand-rolled** — `LinearGradient` on `elevated` tokens + `ElevatedEdges` + `Layout.shadow.card`, radius `control` (10) |
| `ExportCaseCard.tsx` | **hand-rolled** — `View(wrapper) + LinearGradient + View(highlight)`, radius `lg` (12) |
| `NewCaseModal` / `NewLocationModal` / `DuplicateLocationModal` / `EditIncidentLocationModal` / `CaseActionsSheet` headers | **hand-rolled** `LinearGradient` on `GlassColors[scheme].elevated`, no radius (full-bleed pageSheet header) |
| `AutocompleteSuggestionList.tsx` | **hand-rolled** — flat `colors.background` + `colors.border`, radius `md` (8), lift from `Layout.shadow.card[colorScheme]` |
| `ExportHub.tsx` footer | **hand-rolled** `LinearGradient` on `GlassColors[scheme].header` |

**Why the hand-rolls survive** — the reasons are written in-file, verbatim:

- Nested rows (`LocationItem.tsx:83-87`, `CompactLocationItem.tsx:98-102`): *"`Card` paints it outside the gradient in a clipping wrapper; the same shape is reproduced here because Card pins its gradient to radius `lg` and cannot express the nested tier's `md` (D13 / DEF-UI-008). Every value below still comes from Card's tokens."*
- `CoordinateDisplay.tsx:144-146`: *"Top highlight edge, same shape `Card` paints outside its gradient. Reproduced here rather than reusing `Card` because this surface is pressable (hold to copy) and `Card` takes no press handlers."*
- `ExportCaseCard.tsx:119-124`: *"Shadow lives on the WRAPPER, not the gradient: `card` needs `overflow:'hidden'` for the gradient's rounded corners, and on iOS masksToBounds clips the layer's OWN shadow (CSS box-shadow survives an element's overflow:hidden; UIKit doesn't — PR-91 MEDIUM). The wrapper's opaque background lets iOS use the cheap shadowPath instead of rasterizing every card on scroll."*
- `ExportCaseCard.tsx:138-141`: *"Top highlight edge, the 1px strip every other glass surface in the app carries (Card, FormSection, GlassBottomSheet). It lives INSIDE the gradient rather than on the wrapper because only the gradient may take overflow:'hidden' — see the wrapper comment."*

**Glass token values** (`src/constants/Colors.ts`, `GlassColors`) that my files index into:

`nestedCard` in DARK is the SAME two stops as `card`, **swapped** (Colors.ts:363-379): *"the stops are SWAPPED, so the surface is lit from above instead of from below. Same two values, so every contrast number in the palette contract is byte-identical — this is free."* The fill cannot lift: `textTertiary` measures exactly **3.79** on the lighter stop, which is the floor `palette-contrast.test.ts` pins under ruling **M2(b)**. Border goes dE 3.1 → **14.7**; `highlightTop` dE 4.0 → **12.9** (it was 0.06 alpha, "which is to say it was not rendering at all").

`nestedCard` in LIGHT nests **downward** (Colors.ts:286-301) — `card` is already `#f8fafc`, no headroom toward white. Held back from a deeper tone (dE 6.46) by `textTertiary`, a documented ceiling: that tone drops it to **3.80** against a **3.79** floor, a 0.01 margin. Shipped values measure dE **2.91 / 5.66** with `textTertiary` at **3.87**.

```ts
/**

export const DATABASE_NAME = 'cctv_recovery.db'

  LAST_CASE_ID: 'case_management:last_case_id',
  LAST_LOCATION_ID: 'case_management:last_location_id',
} as const)

/**
 * expo-secure-store key holding the SQLCipher database encryption key.
 *
 * Separate from STORAGE_KEYS (AsyncStorage, non-sensitive) — this one lives in
 * the hardware-backed keychain/keystore and is the ONLY thing standing between
 * the encrypted .db file and its contents. Lose it and the database is
 * cryptographically gone, not merely damaged.
 *
 * NO COLON. SecureStore key names must match /^[\w.-]+$/ — alphanumerics, ".",
 * "-", "_" only. The validator is JS-side and throws BEFORE any native call, so
 * an invalid name fails on every launch, on both platforms
 * (node_modules/expo-secure-store/src/SecureStore.ts:237 `isValidKey`).
 *
 * Do NOT copy the colon convention from STORAGE_KEYS above — that is
 * AsyncStorage, which has no such restriction. Doing exactly that shipped
 * BUG-020: 'case_management:db_encryption_key' bricked database init on device
 * while the whole test suite stayed green. Matches the working SecureStore
```

**The severity trio** (CaseStatusBadge.tsx:117-128):

```ts
function severityConfig(
  label: string,
  severity: 'warning' | 'info' | 'success',
  colors: ThemeColors,
): StatusConfig {
  return {
    label,
    backgroundColor: colors[`${severity}Light`],
    borderColor: colors[severity],
    textColor: colors[`${severity}OnLight`],
  }
}
```

**The neutral** (CaseStatusBadge.tsx:130-138):

```ts
/** Archived / Unknown: the absence of a severity, and deliberately grey. */
function neutralConfig(label: string, colors: ThemeColors): StatusConfig {
  return {
    label,
    backgroundColor: withAlpha(colors.textSecondary, NEUTRAL_TINT_ALPHA),
    borderColor: colors.border,
    textColor: colors.text,
  }
}
```

with `const NEUTRAL_TINT_ALPHA = 0.15` (CaseStatusBadge.tsx:30).

**The switch** (CaseStatusBadge.tsx:140-167):

```ts
function getStatusConfig(status: CaseStatus | LocationStatus, colors: ThemeColors): StatusConfig {
  switch (status) {
    // ===== CASE STATUSES =====
    case CaseStatus.DRAFT:
      // Display as "Active" even though enum is still DRAFT
      // Full enum rename deferred to follow-up PR
      return severityConfig('Active', 'warning', colors)
    case CaseStatus.COMPLETE:
      return severityConfig('Complete', 'success', colors)
    case CaseStatus.ARCHIVED:
      return neutralConfig('Archived', colors)

    // ===== LOCATION STATUSES =====
    case LocationStatus.STARTED:
      return severityConfig('Started', 'warning', colors)
    case LocationStatus.WORKING:
      return severityConfig('Working', 'info', colors)
    case LocationStatus.COMPLETE:
      return severityConfig('Complete', 'success', colors)

    default:
      return neutralConfig('Unknown', colors)
  }
}
```

**In dark mode all four `*OnLight` tokens are byte-identical `#f0f4f8`.** That is the single most load-bearing fact for a web replica: dark-mode status is carried by the **fill + border pair only**, never the foreground.

**What it replaced.** `git show d9606460:src/features/case-management/components/CaseStatusBadge.tsx` — 111 lines, no border at all, `borderRadius: 12` as a raw literal, `paddingVertical: size === 'small' ? 2 : size === 'large' ? 6 : 4`, `paddingHorizontal: size === 'small' ? 6 : size === 'large' ? 12 : 8`, and this fill/text scheme:

| Status | Baseline fill | Baseline text |
|---|---|---|
| DRAFT | `colors.warning + '20'` | `colors.warning` |
| COMPLETE (case) | `colors.success + '20'` | `colors.success` |
| ARCHIVED | `colors.textSecondary + '20'` | `colors.textSecondary` |
| STARTED | `colors.warning + '20'` | `colors.warning` |
| WORKING | `colors.primary + '20'` | `colors.primary` |
| COMPLETE (loc) | `colors.success + '20'` | `colors.success` |
| default | `colors.textSecondary + '20'` | `colors.textSecondary` |

i.e. a hex-append 12.5% (`'20'` = 0x20/255 ≈ 0.125) translucent tint of the SATURATED accent, with the same saturated accent as the label, no border, no `testID` prop, and no `Layout` import at all.

**Notes — the in-file design record, quoted.**

File header, lines 1-10:
> *"Visual indicator for case/location status, and the app's only one - six call sites across the Cases, Dashboard and Export tabs. Takes `Banner.tsx`'s severity recipe (`*Light` fill + `colors[severity]` border + `*OnLight` text). See `getStatusConfig` for why the fill is opaque and why the border is load-bearing rather than decorative."*

Lines 21-29, on why only the neutral is a tint:
> *"Alpha for the NEUTRAL tint only (Archived / Unknown). Those two are the absence of a severity rather than a fourth one, so they get a grey wash of `textSecondary` instead of a `*Light` tone — deliberately the one status treatment that does NOT carry a hue. Every other status now takes the opaque `*Light` fill (see below); this used to tint all six, which is what collapsed the colour code."*

Lines 101-116 — the D8(a) ruling, the opacity argument and the two-carrier argument, with numbers:
> *"The severity trio for a status that HAS one: opaque `*Light` fill, `colors[severity]` border, `*OnLight` text. This is `Banner.tsx`'s recipe - the same thing at notice scale - and it is what ruling **D8(a)** built the `*Light` / `*OnLight` pair for.*
> *Opaque, not a tint. D8(a)'s contrast guarantee is measured against the `*Light` tone exactly; a translucent wash composites over whatever glass tier the badge lands on and cannot be measured. It also cannot carry a hue: **at 15% over the dark nested-card ground the accents land within CIE76 dE 3.8-8.9 of one another**, which is why every chip read grey.*
> *The border is a SECOND carrier, not decoration: **in dark mode all four `*OnLight` tokens resolve to `#f0f4f8`**, so the foreground carries no status there and the fill+border pair has to. Banner documents the same split."*

Lines 156-160 — why WORKING is `info` and not `primary`:
> *"`info`, not `primary`. D8(a) only created the `*Light`/`*OnLight` pair for the four severities and `primary` is not one of them, so the D8 pass fell back to the neutral `colors.text` here - which made Working byte-identical to Archived and Unknown. `map-view`'s STATUS_SEVERITY had already resolved the same gap the same way; the two agree now."*

`Colors.ts:83-89` — the measured D8a contrast figures for the `*OnLight` quartet against their own `*Light` backgrounds:
> *"Measured against their own backgrounds: **info 7.15:1, warning 8.15:1, success 6.78:1, error 6.80:1**."*

`Colors.ts:186-194` — dark half:
> *"All four resolve to the standard `#f0f4f8` ... so consumers can write `colors.warningOnLight` without branching on the active scheme. Measured: **info 5.94:1, warning 5.40:1, success 5.93:1, error 5.79:1**."*

**Badge-blue recolor (PR #110 / `68f4e18a feat(theme): land the in-flight badge-blue recolor base`).** The whole dark palette was re-anchored on `background: '#002853'` ("Badge-blue base", Colors.ts:135) with `backgroundSecondary: '#0e3965'` ("Slightly elevated (+6% lightness)", :136) and `card: '#0e3965'` (:212). `primary` became `#2B8CC1` / RGB(43,140,193) (:130). `dark.sheet` (Colors.ts:398-403) is explicitly *"Anchored on the badge-blue ramp, replacing the three competing hand-rolled navies (#0f2035 GlassBottomSheet, #04305c TimePicker, #0b1624 MediaLibrarySheet) that shipped alongside it."* `dark.recessed` (Colors.ts:404-435) was re-anchored later still: it had been `rgb(6,12,22)` / `rgb(10,20,34)` — *"near-black, and on no ramp in this app"* — measuring **16.65 / 11.70 CIE76 dE** from the sheet it sits on, where *"the entire card-on-background separation is 6.7-10.4 dE"*; now **7.87 / 4.01**.

**Ruling D8 in practice.** `*Light` is now a **background tone**, not a lighter accent — Colors.ts marks each one inline: `successLight: '#d1fae5', // Green 100 - background tone (D8)` (:58), `errorLight` (:62), `warningLight` (:66), `infoLight` (:80). Dark says it out loud (Colors.ts:163-164): *"The `*Light` names are historical: in dark mode they are the DARK background tone the matching `*OnLight` foreground sits on (D8a)."* Two dark tones were re-darkened for AA: `successLight: '#0f6b42', // Background tone; was #1a8754 (only 4.10:1)` (:166) and `warningLight: '#7d5f10', // Background tone; was #b38f2f (only 2.76:1)` (:174).

**`warningAccent` (DEF-UI-017).** A fifth token added because the other three severities already had a legible accent (Colors.ts:70-77): *"`warning` 1.76, `warningDark` 2.62, this 4.58. Named rather than theme-branched so consumers write `colors.warningAccent` flat, the same convention as the `*OnLight` quartet."* Light `#b45309` (Amber 700); dark `#ffc62b` — *"a shade that clears (6.82:1 on the worst stop), so this is `warningDark`"* (:178-180).

**DELETED tokens (DEF-UI-010, Colors.ts:237-254).** `accent`, `accentLight`, `accentDark`, `blueprint` are gone. The note records the aliases they collapsed to: `accent = warning`, `blueprint = textSecondary / info`. *"Only `accentLight` / `accentDark` were unique, and nothing rendered them."* A web replica must not reintroduce them.

**Notes — BUG-029, quoted from CaseCard.tsx:187-192:**
> *"A location mutation - rename, re-address, status change - bumps ONLY `locations.updated_at`: `location-service.ts` issues no `UPDATE cases`, there are no SQL triggers, and `locationCount` is a COUNT(*) that a status flip does not move. Without this key the comparator threw away every render that carried a completed location, and the Cases tab showed "Working" forever. `ExportCaseCard` carries the identical key."*

The added comparator key (CaseCard.tsx:193-194):

```js
prevProps.case.locations.map((location) => location.updatedAt).join('|') ===
  nextProps.case.locations.map((location) => location.updatedAt).join('|') &&
```

The twin lives at `ExportCaseCard.tsx:240-241` with its own note (:237-239): *"Location CONTENT key (PR-90 MEDIUM): a location mutation bumps only locations.updated_at — never cases.updated_at or locationCount — so without this a renamed/re-statused row renders stale."*

### `SwipeableCaseCard` — `src/features/case-management/components/SwipeableCaseCard.tsx`

**Status:** CHANGED (196 lines; `git diff --stat` `19 +-` — prettier plus the haptics M4 swap)
**Phase/PR:** `1620dd79 refactor(haptics): drop the now-redundant void/await at safeImpactAsync call sites (M4)` · `d1739700` (prettier)

**Role:** Wraps `CaseCard` in `ReanimatedSwipeable`, renders `SwipeDeleteAction` on the right, and **disables the swipe entirely while the card is expanded**.

**Canonical recipe NOW.** No glass of its own — it is a clipping wrapper. Full style block, verbatim (SwipeableCaseCard.tsx:186-196):

```js
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  swipeableWrapper: {
    overflow: 'hidden',
    borderRadius: Layout.borderRadius.lg,
    // Margin moved here from CaseCard to prevent bottom overflow clipping.
    // Child margins inside overflow: 'hidden' cause delete button overflow.
    marginBottom: Layout.spacing.md,
    // Android requires elevation: 0 for proper overflow clipping on API < 28
    ...(Platform.OS === 'android' && { elevation: 0 }),
  },
})
```

→ `borderRadius: Layout.borderRadius.lg` = **12** (matches `Card`'s glass radius exactly, so the clip does not shave the card's corner), `marginBottom: Layout.spacing.md` = **16**, `overflow:'hidden'`, Android `elevation: 0`.

Swipe config (SwipeableCaseCard.tsx:164-167): `rightThreshold` = **40**, `overshootRight` = **false**, `friction` = **2**, plus `enabled={!isExpanded}` (:167).

Guard (SwipeableCaseCard.tsx:97-112): `renderRightActions` returns `null` outright when `isExpanded`. Haptic fires only when collapsed (:87-95). Accessibility: `accessible={!isExpanded}` (:152), a `delete` accessibility action (:154), and a conditional hint (:156-158) — `'Swipe disabled while expanded'` vs `'Swipe left to delete, or use actions menu'`. Label (:148) reads: *Case {caseNumber}, {locationCount} location(s). Double tap to expand. Swipe left or use actions menu to delete.*

**What it replaced.** Style block byte-identical at baseline. The only functional delta is `void safeImpactAsync()` → `safeImpactAsync()` (M4) and prettier wrapping.

**Notes.** Header comment (:1-7): *"IMPORTANT: Swipe is DISABLED when card is expanded. This prevents accidental deletion when viewing/editing locations."* The `elevation: 0` Android note is an API<28 overflow-clipping workaround, in-file at :193.

```js
      fontFamily: Typography.fontFamily.scannerMono,
      color: colors.textTertiary,
    },
  })
```

**Resolved: `borderRadius: Layout.borderRadius.full` = 9999 — the pill is NOT on the D13 nested-row `md` corner; it is fully rounded.** It takes the nested-row *fill/border tier* (`nestedCard`) but a pill corner. `wrapper` marginRight **8** / marginBottom **4**; `container` paddingVertical **8**, paddingHorizontal **12**, `borderWidth: 1`, `minHeight: Layout.touchTarget.min` = **44**; `dot` **6×6**, radius **9999**, marginRight **6**; `text` **14** / `textSecondary` / `maxWidth: 140` / `numberOfLines={1}`; `moreText` **12** / `'ShareTechMono-Regular'` / `textTertiary`. `activeOpacity={0.7}` on both (:92, :137).

**Status dot colour map** (LocationPill.tsx:41-51) — a LOCAL switch, deliberately not shared:

```js
function getLocationDotColor(status: LocationStatus, colors: ThemeColors): string {
  switch (status) {
    case LocationStatus.COMPLETE:
      return colors.successDark
    case LocationStatus.WORKING:
      return colors.infoDark
    case LocationStatus.STARTED:
    default:
      return colors.warningAccent
  }
}
```

Resolved:

| Status | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|
| `COMPLETE` | `#059669` `successDark` | `#0faa5e` `successDark` |
| `WORKING` | `#2563eb` `infoDark` | `#7a9fc4` `infoDark` |
| `STARTED` / default | `#b45309` `warningAccent` | `#ffc62b` `warningAccent` |

Accessibility labels: `` `Location: ${displayText}, status: ${location.status}` `` (:95) and `` `${count} more locations` `` (:140). `+N` renders as `` {`+${count}`} `` (:149). Display-text precedence (:69-81): `businessName` → `streetAddress` → `locationName` → literal `'Location'`.

**What it replaced.** Baseline (`git show d9606460:...LocationPill.tsx`, style block lines 135-177):

- `container.borderRadius: 20` (raw), `paddingVertical: 8`, `paddingHorizontal: 12`, **no `minHeight`** — the in-file note at :178 records it *"shipped at ~34pt with no hitSlop"*, i.e. below the 44pt floor.
- `container.borderColor: colorScheme === 'dark' ? 'rgba(43, 140, 193, 0.2)' : 'rgba(30, 58, 138, 0.15)'` — a hand-mixed pair, now `nestedCard.border`.
- **No gradient at all on the pill** — baseline `LocationPill` was a bare `View`; the glass gradient is new.
- A SEPARATE `moreContainer` style for `+N`: `paddingVertical: 8, paddingHorizontal: 12, borderRadius: 20, backgroundColor: colorScheme === 'dark' ? colors.backgroundTertiary : colors.backgroundSecondary` — flat fill, **no border**, hence the "one pill and one gap" defect quoted above.
- `dot.borderRadius: 3` (raw), `dot.marginRight: 6` (raw).
- `moreText.fontFamily: 'JetBrainsMono'` — unbundled face.
- Baseline dot colours were the SATURATED accents: `colors.success` / `colors.primary` / `colors.warning`.

**Notes — the WCAG 1.4.11 dot argument, quoted verbatim from LocationPill.tsx:26-40:**
> *"Map location status to dot color. Hoisted to module level to avoid per-render allocation.*
> *The dot is the pill's only visual carrier of status for a sighted user (the `accessibilityLabel` does carry it, so the loss was sighted-users-only), which puts it under **WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 non-text floor**. The saturated `success` / `primary` / `warning` fills it used to read measured **2.08 light, 2.81 dark and 1.76 light** respectively on the `nestedCard`-over-`card` ground the pill paints. These three are the same accents `map-view`'s `STATUS_ACCENT` resolves for the identical mark on the bottom-sheet row, held to the same acceptance bar: **at or above 3:1 on both `card` and `sheet` stops in both themes, four distinct hues**. Kept as a local switch rather than an import because the two live in different features; the shared thing is the TOKENS. (**DEF-UI-017**.)"*

And the one-surface note at :164-169, quoted in the style block above.

### `SwipeDeleteAction` — `src/features/case-management/components/SwipeDeleteAction.tsx`

**Status:** CHANGED (127 lines; `git diff --stat` `43 ++--`)
**Phase/PR:** `3af3c9fe fix(case-management): one rail colour, and the on-error foreground on swipe-delete` · `9801c9e9 fix(case-management): discharge DEF-UI-001's named required action (F2)`

**CONFIRMED: it consumes `DangerFill` from `src/constants/Colors.ts`.** Import at line 23:

```ts
import { DangerFill, ThemeColors } from '@/constants/Colors'
import type { ColorScheme } from '@/constants/Colors'
```

Applied at line 105: `backgroundColor: DangerFill[colorScheme],`.

**Role:** The red panel revealed under a right swipe — trash icon + "Delete", fixed 100pt wide.

**Canonical recipe NOW — full `StyleSheet.create` block, verbatim (SwipeDeleteAction.tsx:87-127):**

```js
const createStyles = (colors: ThemeColors, colorScheme: ColorScheme) =>
  StyleSheet.create({
    container: {
      width: DELETE_BUTTON_WIDTH,
      // `DangerFill`, the shared deep-red recipe, not the flat `colors.error`.
      //
      // DEF-UI-001 attached a NAMED required action to this file: "re-measure
      // `SwipeDeleteAction` after the fix - it is a confirmation-free
      // destructive affordance and the only site where the ratio got worse to
      // get the token right." Applying ruling D7(a) here moved the label from
      // `textInverse` (4.40 dark) to `onError`, which measures 3.34 on this
      // flat fill. Measured, with `onError` at 14px semibold (normal text, no
      // AA-large relief):
      //
      //   flat `error`   3.34 dark / 3.76 light   FAIL
      //   `DangerFill`   6.39 dark / 4.83 light   PASS
      //
      // Same recipe `Button`'s danger variant paints.
      backgroundColor: DangerFill[colorScheme],
      justifyContent: 'center',
      alignItems: 'center',
    },
    touchable: {
      flex: 1,
      justifyContent: 'center',
      alignItems: 'center',
    },
    content: {
      alignItems: 'center',
      justifyContent: 'center',
      gap: Layout.spacing.xs,
    },
    text: {
      // `onError` is the foreground token for a filled destructive surface
      // (D7a). It replaces `textInverse`, which is NAVY in dark mode - a
      // dark-on-red pairing on a confirmation-free destructive affordance.
      color: colors.onError,
      fontSize: Typography.fontSize.sm,
      fontWeight: Typography.fontWeight.semibold,
    },
  })
```

**`DangerFill` definition** (`src/constants/Colors.ts:510-513`):

```ts
export const DangerFill = {
  light: Colors.light.errorDark,
  dark: Colors.dark.errorLight,
} as const
```

**Resolved: light = `#dc2626` (Red 600), dark = `#b72136`.** Foreground `colors.onError` = **`#ffffff` in BOTH themes** (Colors.ts:96, :202).

Other resolved values: `width: DELETE_BUTTON_WIDTH` = **100**, `content.gap: Layout.spacing.xs` = **4**, `text` **14** / `'600'`. Icon (SwipeDeleteAction.tsx:79): `<Ionicons name="trash-outline" size={24} color={colors.onError} />` — **size 24 as a raw literal**, equal to `Layout.iconSize.md`. Label text is the literal `Delete` (:80).

Animation (SwipeDeleteAction.tsx:50-68): container opacity is a fast timed fade — `withTiming(progress.value > 0.05 ? 1 : 0, { duration: 50 })` — while the content scales `interpolate(progress, [0, 0.5, 1], [0.8, 0.95, 1], Extrapolation.CLAMP)`. Pressed state inline (:74): `{ opacity: pressed ? 0.8 : 1 }`.

**What it replaced.** Baseline:

```js
container: { width: DELETE_BUTTON_WIDTH, backgroundColor: colors.error, ... },
text:      { color: colors.textInverse, fontSize: Typography.fontSize.sm, fontWeight: semibold },
```

→ fill `colors.error` (light `#ef4444`, dark `#ff4757`) and label `colors.textInverse`, which is **`#002853` navy in dark mode** — dark-on-red.

**Notes — DEF-UI-001's named required action, quoted from Colors.ts:492-509 (the `DangerFill` docblock):**
> *"The DEEP red a filled destructive control paints, so that `onError` (`#ffffff` in both themes) can clear WCAG AA 4.5:1 on it.*
> *It is a lookup rather than a literal per theme because the `*Light` / `*Dark` names **INVERT** between schemes by design (see the dark block: "in dark mode they are the DARK background tone"). The deep red is therefore `errorDark` in light and `errorLight` in dark, which is the kind of thing every consumer gets wrong once. Measured with `onError`:*
> *  flat `error` (what these sites shipped)   **3.34 dark / 3.76 light   FAIL***
> *  `errorDark` in both                       **4.10 dark / 4.83 light   dark fails***
> *  this pair                                 **6.39 dark / 4.83 light   PASS***
> *Two consumers: `Button`'s danger variant and `SwipeDeleteAction`, which is a confirmation-free destructive affordance and the one site DEF-UI-001 attached a named re-measurement to."*

Rulings named in-file: **D7(a)** (the `onError` foreground for a filled destructive surface) and **DEF-UI-001** / finding **F2**.

```tsx
export interface EmptyStateProps {
  message?: string
  actionLabel?: string
  onActionPress?: () => void
}

export function EmptyState({
  message = 'No cases found',
  actionLabel = 'Create Case',
  onActionPress,
}: EmptyStateProps) {
  const { colors } = useTheme()

  return (
    <View style={styles.container}>
      <Text style={[styles.message, { color: colors.textSecondary }]}>{message}</Text>
      {onActionPress && (
        <Button onPress={onActionPress} variant="primary" style={styles.button}>

        </Button>
      )}
    </View>
  )
}

    paddingVertical: Layout.spacing.xxl,
    alignItems: 'center',
    justifyContent: 'center',
  },
  message: {
    fontSize: Typography.fontSize.lg,
    textAlign: 'center',
    marginBottom: Layout.spacing.lg,
  },
  button: {
    minWidth: 200,
  },
})
```

**No icon, no illustration, no glass surface, no border, no card.** It is a bare centred `View` on whatever ground it lands on. `styles` is a module-level `StyleSheet.create` (not a `createStyles(colors)` factory) — the only theme-dependent value, the message colour, is applied inline at :29.

The action `Button` renders **only when `onActionPress` is supplied**. Neither of the two production consumers in my scope supplies it, so `actionLabel = 'Create Case'` is dead in the Cases/Dashboard paths — the default exists for other callers.
