## 6 Explicitly out of scope for the web port

Everything below appears in `git diff d9606460..main` and is **not** a UI-parity item. Listed so the
matrix-writer does not chase it. Anything not listed here and not in §3.2 **is** in scope.

### 6.1 React-Native-only mechanics with no web analog

| Change | Where | Why it does not port |
|---|---|---|
| `expo-image` migration (`Image` → `expo-image`) | `ConfirmationScreen`, `MediaPreview`, `PhotoList`, others | A caching/decoding swap. Rendered output is unchanged; the web has `next/image`. |
| `@expo/vector-icons` subpath imports + `src/types/expo-vector-icons.d.ts` (new, +17) | repo-wide | Bundle-size plumbing. The **glyph names and sizes** DO port (§2); the import mechanics do not. |
| `safe-haptics` / `expo-haptics` call sites | `Switch`, `ScrollableTextInput`, `SwipeableCaseCard`, others | No web equivalent. Several files are `CHANGED` **only** because of haptics — §3.2 marks them inert. |
| `react-native-reanimated` / `react-native-gesture-handler` API usage | `GlassBottomSheet`, swipeables, `MapBottomSheet` | The **library** does not port. The **motion values do** — e.g. `GlassBottomSheet`'s RN `slide` → Reanimated 260 ms in / 200 ms out fade-plus-travel. Treat timings as in-scope, APIs as out. |
| Safe-area insets (`react-native-safe-area-context`) | `GlassBottomSheet`, headers, tab bar | Device chrome. The demo's phone frame is fixed. |
| `expo-system-ui`, `userInterfaceStyle`, native permissions arrays | `app.config.js` | Native config. **Exception:** `app.config.js`'s three `#002853` sites, which are the native half of ruling D5(a) — see §1.7; only the three JS sites matter to the web. |
| `npx expo prebuild` + fresh dev build | outstanding owner task | Native rebuild for D5(a). |
| VisionCamera / `expo-camera` surfaces | `VisionCameraScreen`, `PermissionsView`, `ModeToggle`, `RecordingIndicator`, OCR `CameraScreen` | The demo has no live camera. **But the OCR camera-step CHROME is a real UI surface the demo stubs** — its bounding box, instructions and capture button all changed (§2.G) and those are portable. Judge per surface, not per feature. |
| `expo-local-authentication` / biometrics | `AuthenticationProvider`, `useBiometric`, `biometric-service` | Real auth is out per the v1 owner scope. The **splash / lock / HUD chrome** is a separate question (§2.B). |
| SQLite, filesystem, `expo-sharing`, ZIP | `services/` throughout | Logic, not UI. |

The **`no em dashes in user-facing strings`** rule (§5.1, addendum 2) is a phone-side copy rule, and
this document is exempt from it. But the *strings themselves* are parity surface: nine settings
strings, five wizard strings and three media strings changed wording between baseline and `main`
(§2.E, §2.F, §2.G). Port the new wording. Note also that **three em dashes survive at `main`** in
`EnrollmentQRModal.tsx:71`, `OrgPlanStep.tsx:65-70` and `TokenStep.tsx:57-59` (all agency-cloud, all
out of scope anyway) and that PR #127 introduced a **new** violation at
`VisionCameraScreen.tsx:679` — `"No location permission — captures will have no GPS. Tap to grant."`
Do not replicate that one; do not "fix" the surviving three in the demo either, since those screens
are out of scope.

## 7 Measured contrast ratios the port must meet

**Provenance rule, stated once.** `docs/plans/ui-consistency/03-SESSION-RUNBOOK.md:161` is explicit: *"All ratios are computed-not-observed until this runs"*, referring to a consolidated device pass that covers the recorder in light mode (#116), the map sheet, the `TextInput`/scanner rows (#123) and the OCR permission gate. **That consolidated pass never ran.** The one device pass that *did* run is PR #125's four owner-verified rounds on a physical iPhone, whose outcome is `docs/plans/ui-touchups/code-reviews/PR-125/DEVICE-PASS.md`. Everything below is therefore **COMPUTED** unless the last column says otherwise.

Thresholds throughout: **AA 4.5:1** for normal-size text and **3:1** for the non-text graphics of WCAG 1.4.11. There is no AA-large relief anywhere in the campaign's measurements: the largest type involved is 16px semibold, which is normal size (`palette-contrast.test.ts:18-20`).

The demo is **dark-only**, so the "Dark-relevant?" column is the filter to read first.

---

### 7.1 The machine-checked contract — `src/constants/__tests__/palette-contrast.test.ts`

This file is the authoritative set: it imports the real constants (deep imports on purpose, so the pin moves *with* the value it guards) and recomputes with a WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance implementation that does **alpha compositing over the real two-stop gradient stacks**, not over a flat approximation. All 464 lines are NEW since the baseline.

**The grounds it measures against** (`:137-158`) — this is the actual surface stack, and a web port that measures against a flat hex will get different numbers:

- `DARK_GROUNDS` = `background` · both stops of `card` over background · both stops of `nestedCard` over `card`'s lower stop over background · both stops of `sheet` over background · both stops of `recessed` over `sheet`'s upper stop over background.
- `LIGHT_GROUNDS` = the same shape without the opaque background under it (light `card` is already opaque).
- `worst(fg, grounds)` = the **minimum** across every one of those grounds.

**Two pins the port should copy structurally, not just numerically:**
- The `DangerFill` lesson (`:265-274`): `SwipeDeleteAction`'s own tests compared the rendered value against `DangerFill.*` itself, so they moved *with* the constant and stayed 32/32 green through a mutation back to the failing pair. Pin the ratio at the constant, not at a consumer.
- The `recessed` two-sided ΔE bound (`:343-374`): "too flat" and "too deep" are both bugs, and every gradient stop is bounded **independently** — taking `Math.max` meant the lower bound only fired when *both* stops went flat.

The load-bearing insight, and it ports directly: **on a blue gradient the two candidate label colours move in opposite directions**, so there is no stop where both clear 4.5:1. Pick the foreground first, then tune the gradient to it.
